sentences.zh: 王治，字本道，忻州人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi, style Bendao, was a native of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi, styled Bendao, came from Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十二年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-second year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 除行人，遷吏科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Courier, then transferred to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier, then promoted to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel section.

sentences.zh: 寇屢盜邊，邊臣多匿不奏；

translations.literal: Bandits repeatedly raided the borders, and frontier officials often concealed this and did not report it;
translations.idiomatic: Raiders struck the frontier again and again, yet border officials often hushed it up and filed no reports;

sentences.zh: 小勝，文臣輒冒軍功。

translations.literal: after minor victories, civil officials would claim military merit.
translations.idiomatic: after the slightest success, civil officials would claim military credit for themselves.

sentences.zh: 治請臨陣斬獲，第錄將士功；

translations.literal: Zhi requested that kills and captures in battle be credited only to officers and soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi petitioned that battlefield kills and captures be credited only to officers and soldiers;

sentences.zh: 文臣及鎮帥不親搏戰者止賜賚。

translations.literal: civil officials and regional commanders who did not fight in person should receive only rewards and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: civil officials and regional commanders who did not fight in person should receive only stipends and gifts.

sentences.zh: 從之，再遷禮科左給事中。

translations.literal: The request was granted, and he was again transferred to Left Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Rites section.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed, and he was soon promoted to Left Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Rites section.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年，偕御史王好問核內府諸監局歲費。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing, together with Censor Wang Haowen he audited the annual expenditures of the various directorates and offices of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longqing, he joined Censor Wang Haowen in auditing the annual costs of the inner-palace directorates and offices.

sentences.zh: 中官崔敏請止之，為給事中張憲臣所劾。

translations.literal: Eunuch Cui Min asked that the audit be stopped and was impeached by Supervising Secretary Zhang Xianchen.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Cui Min asked that the audit be halted and was impeached by Supervising Secretary Zhang Xianchen.

sentences.zh: 得旨：「詔書所載者，自嘉靖四十一年始，聽治等詳核。

translations.literal: An edict was received: "What is recorded in the imperial proclamation shall be audited in detail by Zhi and the others beginning from the forty-first year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: An edict came down: "Items listed in the imperial proclamation are to be audited in detail by Zhi and his colleagues from the forty-first year of Jiajing onward.

sentences.zh: 不載者，已之。」

translations.literal: What is not recorded shall be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: What is not listed is to be discontinued."

sentences.zh: 治等力爭，不許。

translations.literal: Zhi and the others argued strenuously, but were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and his colleagues protested vigorously, but the court would not yield.

sentences.zh: 事竣，劾中官趙廷玉、馬尹幹沒罪，詔下司禮監按問。

translations.literal: When the matter was concluded, they impeached eunuchs Zhao Tingyu and Ma Yin for embezzlement; an edict ordered the Directorate of Ceremonial to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When the audit was finished, they impeached the eunuchs Zhao Tingyu and Ma Yin for embezzlement, and an edict sent the case to the Directorate of Ceremonial for inquiry.

sentences.zh: 尋上疏陳四事：「一、定宗廟之禮以隆聖孝。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he submitted a memorial setting forth four matters: "First, fix the ancestral temple rites to exalt sagely filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized on four matters: "First, settle the ancestral temple rites to exalt filial devotion to the sages.

sentences.zh: 獻皇雖貴為天子父，未嘗南面臨天下；

translations.literal: Although the Xian Emperor was honored as the emperor's father, he never faced south and ruled all under Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Although the Xian Emperor was honored as the emperor's father, he never faced south to rule the realm;

sentences.zh: 雖親為武宗叔，然嘗北面事武宗。

translations.literal: although he was the Jiajing Emperor's uncle by blood, he had once faced north in service to the Wuzong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: though he was the Jiajing Emperor's uncle, he had once faced north in service to Emperor Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 今乃與祖宗諸帝並列，設位於武宗右，揆諸古典，終為未協。

translations.literal: Now he is ranked alongside the emperors of old and given a place to the right of Wuzong; measured against ancient precedent, this is ultimately not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Now he is ranked with the dynastic founders and given a place to Emperor Wuzong's right—a placement that, by ancient precedent, remains out of keeping.

sentences.zh: 臣以為獻皇祔會太廟，不免遞遷。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that if the Xian Emperor is enshrined in the Grand Ancestral Temple, he cannot avoid being moved aside in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject believes that if the Xian Emperor is enshrined in the Grand Ancestral Temple, he cannot escape eventual displacement.

sentences.zh: 若專祀世廟，則億世不改。

translations.literal: If he is worshipped solely in the Shrine of Generations, then for ten thousand generations there will be no change.
translations.idiomatic: If he is worshipped solely in the Shrine of Generations, the arrangement will stand for all time.

sentences.zh: 乞敕廷臣博議，務求至當。

translations.literal: I beg that Your Majesty order the court ministers to debate broadly and strive for what is most fitting.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty order the court to debate the matter broadly until the most fitting arrangement is found.

sentences.zh: 一、謹燕居之禮以澄化源。

translations.literal: Second, observe carefully the rites of daily repose to clarify the source of transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Second, observe the rites of daily repose with care to keep the source of moral transformation clear.

sentences.zh: 人主深居禁掖，左右便佞窺伺百出，或以燕飲聲樂，或以遊戲騎射。

translations.literal: The ruler dwells deep within the forbidden quarters, and fawning attendants on every side watch for openings—sometimes with banquets, music, and song, sometimes with games, riding, and archery.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler dwells deep within the forbidden quarters, where fawning attendants watch for every opening—sometimes with banquets and music, sometimes with games, riding, and archery.

sentences.zh: 近則損敝精神，疾病所由生。

translations.literal: In the near term this wears down the spirit, and illness is thereby born.
translations.idiomatic: In the short run it drains the spirit and breeds illness.

sentences.zh: 久則妨累政事，危亂所由起。

translations.literal: Over time it obstructs government, and peril and disorder thereby arise.
translations.idiomatic: Over time it obstructs government and opens the way to peril and disorder.

sentences.zh: 比者人言籍籍，謂陛下燕閑舉動，有非諒闇所宜者。

translations.literal: Recently talk has been rife that Your Majesty's leisurely pursuits and conduct include things unsuitable during the period of filial mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Lately rumor has been rife that Your Majesty's leisure and conduct include things unsuited to a period of filial mourning.

sentences.zh: 臣竊為陛下慮之。」

translations.literal: Your subject ventures to worry on Your Majesty's behalf."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject ventures to worry on Your Majesty's behalf."

sentences.zh: 其二，請勤朝講、親輔弼。

translations.literal: The second and third points urged diligent court sessions and lectures, and close reliance on chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His second and third points urged diligent attendance at court and the Classics Lectern, and close reliance on chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the court merely acknowledged receipt.

sentences.zh: 進吏科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel section.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel section.

sentences.zh: 劾薊遼總督都御史劉燾、南京督儲都御史曾於拱不職，於拱遂罷。

translations.literal: He impeached Regional Commander of Jizhou and Liaodong, Censor-in-Chief Liu Tao, and Nanjing Grain Storage Supervisor, Censor-in-Chief Zeng Yugong, for dereliction; Yugong was then dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Liu Tao, Censor-in-Chief and regional commander of Jizhou and Liaodong, and Zeng Yugong, Nanjing grain-storage supervisor, for dereliction of duty; Yugong was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 山西及薊鎮並中寇，治以罪兵部尚書郭乾、侍郎遲鳳翔，偕同官歐陽一敬等劾之。

translations.literal: Shanxi and Jizhou garrison alike suffered raids; Zhi held Minister of War Guo Qian and Vice Minister Chi Fengxiang responsible, and together with his colleague Ouyang Yijing and others impeached them.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanxi and the Jizhou garrison alike were raided, Zhi blamed Minister of War Guo Qian and Vice Minister Chi Fengxiang and, with his colleague Ouyang Yijing and others, impeached them.

sentences.zh: 詔罷乾，貶鳳翔三秩視事。

translations.literal: An edict dismissed Qian and demoted Fengxiang three ranks while keeping him on duty.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dismissed Qian and demoted Fengxiang three ranks while leaving him in office.

sentences.zh: 部議恤光祿少卿馬從謙。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated posthumous honors for Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Ma Congqian.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry deliberated posthumous honors for Ma Congqian, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，治疏爭。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it, and Zhi memorialized in protest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, and Zhi memorialized in protest.

sentences.zh: 帝謂從謙所犯，比子罵父律，終不允。

translations.literal: The emperor said Congqian's offense was comparable to the statute on a son cursing his father, and in the end did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said Congqian's offense was comparable to the statute on a son cursing his father, and would not relent.

sentences.zh: 治又請追謚何瑭，雪夏言罪，且言大理卿朱廷立、刑部侍郎詹瀚共鍛成夏言、曾銑獄，宜追奪其官。

translations.literal: Zhi again asked that He Tang be granted a posthumous title, that Xia Yan's guilt be cleared, and further said that Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Zhu Tingli and Vice Minister of Justice Zhan Han had together forged the cases of Xia Yan and Zeng Xian, and that their offices should be posthumously revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi again asked that He Tang receive a posthumous title and Xia Yan's guilt be cleared, and charged that Chief Judge Zhu Tingli and Vice Minister of Justice Zhan Han had together forged the cases against Xia Yan and Zeng Xian—offices that should be posthumously revoked.

sentences.zh: 鹹報可。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 明年，左右有言南海子之勝者，帝將往幸。

translations.literal: The next year, attendants spoke of the charms of the Southern Park, and the emperor was about to visit it.
translations.idiomatic: The next year attendants praised the charms of the Southern Park, and the emperor prepared to visit it.

sentences.zh: 治率同官諫，大學士徐階、尚書楊博、御史郝傑等並阻止，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Zhi led his colleagues in remonstrance; Grand Secretary Xu Jie, Minister Yang Bo, Censor Hao Jie, and others also tried to stop him, but none were heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi led his colleagues in remonstrance; Grand Secretary Xu Jie, Minister Yang Bo, Censor Hao Jie, and others joined in trying to stop him, but none were heeded.

sentences.zh: 至則荒莽沮濕，帝甚悔之。

translations.literal: When he arrived it was wild, overgrown, and damp, and the emperor deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived he found only wilderness and bog, and deeply regretted the trip.

sentences.zh: 治尋擢太僕少卿，改大理，進太僕卿。

translations.literal: Zhi was soon promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, transferred to the Court of Judicial Review, and advanced to Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was soon promoted to Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, transferred to the Court of Judicial Review, and then advanced to Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 憂歸，卒。

translations.literal: He returned home in mourning and died.
translations.idiomatic: He went home on mourning leave and died there.

sentences.zh: 歐陽一敬，字司直，彭澤人。

translations.literal: Ouyang Yijing, style Sizhi, was a native of Pengze.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Yijing, styled Sizhi, came from Pengze.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十八年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 除蕭山知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Xiaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Xiaoshan.

sentences.zh: 征授刑科給事中。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Justice section.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Justice section.

sentences.zh: 劾太常少卿晉應槐為文選郎時劣狀，而南京侍郎傅頤、寧夏巡撫王崇古、湖廣參政孫弘軾由應槐進，俱當罷。

translations.literal: He impeached Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Jin Yinghuai for misconduct when he had been a selection secretary, and said that Nanjing Vice Minister Fu Yi, Ningxia Grand Coordinator Wang Chonggu, and Huguang Administration Vice Commissioner Sun Hongshi, all advanced through Yinghuai, should likewise be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Jin Yinghuai, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, for misconduct when he had served as a selection secretary, and argued that Nanjing Vice Minister Fu Yi, Ningxia Grand Coordinator Wang Chonggu, and Huguang Administration Vice Commissioner Sun Hongshi—all promoted through Yinghuai—should be dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 吏部為應槐等辨，獨罷頤官。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel defended Yinghuai and the others, and only Yi was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel defended Yinghuai and the others, and only Yi lost his post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，劾罷禮部尚書董份。

translations.literal: Before long he impeached and brought about the dismissal of Minister of Rites Dong Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he impeached and brought about the dismissal of Minister of Rites Dong Fen.

sentences.zh: 三遷兵科給事中。

translations.literal: After three transfers he became supervising secretary in the Ministry of War section.
translations.idiomatic: After three transfers he became supervising secretary in the Ministry of War section.

sentences.zh: 言廣西總兵當用都督，不當用勛臣。

translations.literal: He said the regional commander of Guangxi should be a regional military commissioner and not a meritorious noble.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that Guangxi's regional commander should be a regional military commissioner, not a meritorious noble.

sentences.zh: 因劾恭順侯吳繼爵，罷之，以俞大猷代。

translations.literal: He therefore impeached the Marquis of Gongshun, Wu Jijue, who was dismissed and replaced by Yu Dayou.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore impeached Wu Jijue, Marquis of Gongshun, who was dismissed and replaced by Yu Dayou.

sentences.zh: 寇大入陜西，劾總督陳其學、巡撫戴才，俱奪官。

translations.literal: When bandits made a major incursion into Shaanxi, he impeached Regional Commander Chen Qixue and Grand Coordinator Dai Cai, and both were stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders made a major incursion into Shaanxi, he impeached Regional Commander Chen Qixue and Grand Coordinator Dai Cai, and both were stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 又以軍政劾英國公張溶，山西、浙江總兵官董一奎、劉顯，掌錦衣衛都督李隆等九人不職。

translations.literal: He also impeached on military grounds the Duke of Ying, Zhang Rong, the regional commanders of Shanxi and Zhejiang Dong Yikui and Liu Xian, the Embroidered Uniform Guard Commissioner Li Long, and nine others in all for dereliction.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached on military grounds the Duke of Ying, Zhang Rong; the regional commanders of Shanxi and Zhejiang, Dong Yikui and Liu Xian; Embroidered Uniform Guard Commissioner Li Long; and nine others in all for dereliction.

sentences.zh: 溶留，余俱貶黜。

translations.literal: Rong was retained; the rest were all demoted or dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was kept in post; the rest were demoted or dismissed.

sentences.zh: 自嚴嵩敗，言官爭發憤論事，一敬尤敢言。

translations.literal: After Yan Song's fall, remonstrance officials vied to speak out in indignation on public affairs; Yijing was especially bold.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan Song's fall, remonstrance officials vied to speak out in indignation on public affairs; Yijing was especially bold.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年正月，吏部尚書楊博掌京察，黜給事中鄭欽、御史胡維新，而山西人無下考者。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Longqing, Minister of Personnel Yang Bo presided over the metropolitan evaluation, demoting Supervising Secretary Zheng Qin and Censor Hu Weixin, while no Shanxi man received a low rating.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Longqing 1, Minister of Personnel Yang Bo presided over the metropolitan evaluation, demoting Supervising Secretary Zheng Qin and Censor Hu Weixin, while no Shanxi man received a low rating.

sentences.zh: 吏科給事中胡應嘉劾博挾私憤，庇鄉里。

translations.literal: Hu Yingjia, supervising secretary of the Personnel Section, impeached Bo for acting on private resentment and shielding men of his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yingjia, supervising secretary of the Personnel Section, impeached Yang Bo for acting on private resentment and shielding men of his native place.

sentences.zh: 應嘉先嘗劾高拱，拱修郤，將重罪之。

translations.literal: Yingjia had earlier impeached Gao Gong; Gong nursed a grudge and was about to punish him severely.
translations.idiomatic: Yingjia had earlier impeached Gao Gong; Gong nursed a grudge and was about to punish him severely.

sentences.zh: 徐階等重違拱意，且以應嘉實佐察，初未言，今黨同官妄奏，擬旨斥為民。

translations.literal: Xu Jie and others strongly went against Gong's intent; moreover, because Yingjia had in fact assisted the evaluation and had said nothing at first, they now joined colleagues in a reckless memorial and drafted an edict to dismiss him as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jie and others strongly went against Gao Gong's intent; moreover, because Yingjia had in fact assisted the evaluation and had said nothing at first, they now joined colleagues in a reckless memorial and drafted an edict to dismiss him as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 言路大嘩。

translations.literal: The remonstrance circuit erupted in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrance circuit erupted in uproar.

sentences.zh: 一敬為應嘉訟，斥博及拱。

translations.literal: Yijing pleaded Yingjia's case and denounced both Bo and Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Yijing pleaded Yingjia's case and denounced both Yang Bo and Gao Gong.

sentences.zh: 詆拱奸險橫惡，無異蔡京，且言：「應嘉前疏臣與聞，黜應嘉不若黜臣。」

translations.literal: He denounced Gong as treacherous, dangerous, overbearing, and wicked—no different from Cai Jing—and said: "I was privy to Yingjia's earlier memorial; dismissing Yingjia would be less fitting than dismissing me."
translations.idiomatic: He denounced Gao Gong as treacherous, dangerous, overbearing, and wicked—no different from Cai Jing—and said, "I was privy to Yingjia's earlier memorial; dismissing Yingjia would be less fitting than dismissing me."

sentences.zh: 會給事中辛自修、御史陳聯芳疏爭，階乃調應嘉建寧推官。

translations.literal: When Supervising Secretary Xin Zixiu and Censor Chen Lianfang memorialized in protest, Jie then transferred Yingjia to investigating censor of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: When Supervising Secretary Xin Zixiu and Censor Chen Lianfang memorialized in protest, Xu Jie then transferred Yingjia to investigating censor of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 一敬尋劾拱威制朝紳，專柄擅國，亟宜罷。

translations.literal: Yijing soon impeached Gong for overawing court officials, monopolizing power, and usurping the state—urgently to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yijing soon impeached Gao Gong for overawing court officials, monopolizing power, and usurping the state, urging his immediate dismissal.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 逾月，御史齊康劾階。

translations.literal: A month later Censor Qi Kang impeached Jie.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Censor Qi Kang impeached Xu Jie.

sentences.zh: 諸給事御史以康受拱指，群集闕下，詈而唾之。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries and censors, believing Kang acted on Gong's instructions, gathered below the palace gate, cursed him, and spat on him.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretaries and censors, believing Kang acted on Gao Gong's instructions, gathered below the palace gate, cursed him, and spat on him.

sentences.zh: 一敬首劾康，康亦劾一敬。

translations.literal: Yijing was the first to impeach Kang, and Kang also impeached Yijing.
translations.idiomatic: Yijing was the first to impeach Kang, and Kang also impeached Yijing.

sentences.zh: 時康主拱，一敬主階，互指為黨。

translations.literal: At the time Kang championed Gong and Yijing championed Jie; each side accused the other of faction.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Kang championed Gao Gong and Yijing championed Xu Jie; each side accused the other of faction.

sentences.zh: 言官多論康，康竟坐謫。

translations.literal: Most remonstrance officials condemned Kang, and Kang was ultimately demoted on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Most remonstrance officials condemned Kang, and Kang was ultimately demoted on that account.

sentences.zh: 已，陳兵政八事，部皆議行。

translations.literal: Thereafter he set forth eight matters on military administration, and the ministry deliberated and adopted them all.
translations.idiomatic: He then set forth eight proposals on military administration, and the ministry adopted them all.

sentences.zh: 南京振武營兵由此罷。

translations.literal: The soldiers of Nanjing's Zhenwu Battalion were thereby abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers of Nanjing's Zhenwu Battalion were abolished as a result.

sentences.zh: 湖廣巡按陳省劾太和山守備中官呂祥，詔征祥還，罷守備官。

translations.literal: Huguang touring censor Chen Sheng impeached the eunuch defender of Mount Taihe, Lü Xiang; an edict recalled Xiang and abolished the defender post.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang touring censor Chen Sheng impeached Lü Xiang, the eunuch defender of Mount Taihe; an edict recalled Xiang and abolished the defender post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復遣監丞劉進往代。

translations.literal: Before long a supervising secretary, Liu Jin, was again sent to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Supervising Secretary Liu Jin was sent to replace him.

sentences.zh: 一敬言：「進故名俊，守顯陵無狀。

translations.literal: Yijing said: "Jin's former name was Jun; he served at the Xian Mausoleum with misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yijing said, "Jin's former name was Jun; he served at the Xian Mausoleum with grave misconduct.

sentences.zh: 肅皇帝下之獄，充孝陵衛凈軍，今不宜用。」

translations.literal: The Jiajing Emperor sent him to prison and made him a purifying soldier of the Xiaoling guard; he should not be used now."
translations.idiomatic: The Jiajing Emperor sent him to prison and made him a purifying soldier of the Xiaoling guard; he must not be appointed now."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 中官呂用等典京營，一敬力諫，事寢。

translations.literal: The eunuchs Lü Yong and others were put in charge of the capital garrison; Yijing remonstrated forcefully, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuchs Lü Yong and others were put in charge of the capital garrison, Yijing remonstrated forcefully and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 黔國公沐朝弼殘恣，屢抗詔旨。

translations.literal: The Duke of Qian, Mu Chaobi, was cruel and willful and repeatedly defied imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Chaobi, Duke of Qian, was cruel and willful and repeatedly defied imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 一敬請治其罪，報可。

translations.literal: Yijing asked that he be punished; approval was returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yijing asked that he be punished, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 俄擢太常少卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 拱再起柄政，一敬懼，即日告歸，半道以憂死。

translations.literal: When Gong again rose to wield power, Yijing was afraid, resigned that very day, and died of grief on the road halfway home.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Gong again seized power, Yijing was afraid, resigned that very day, and died of grief on the road home.

sentences.zh: 時應嘉已屢遷參議，憂歸，聞拱再相，亦驚怖而卒。

translations.literal: At that time Yingjia had already been promoted several times to administration commissioner; he returned home in mourning, and on hearing that Gong was again chief minister, he too died of fright.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yingjia had already risen several times to administration commissioner; he was home on mourning leave, and on hearing that Gao Gong was chief minister again, he too died of fright.

sentences.zh: 應嘉，沐陽人。

translations.literal: Yingjia was a native of Muyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yingjia came from Muyang.

sentences.zh: 由宜春知縣擢吏科給事中。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Yichun he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel section.
translations.idiomatic: From magistrate of Yichun he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel section.

sentences.zh: 三遷都給事中。

translations.literal: After three transfers he became chief supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After three transfers he became chief supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 論侍郎黃養蒙、李登雲及布政使李磐、侯一元不職，皆罷去。

translations.literal: He charged Vice Ministers Huang Yangmeng and Li Dengyun and administration commissioners Li Pan and Hou Yiyuan with dereliction, and all were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He charged Vice Ministers Huang Yangmeng and Li Dengyun and administration commissioners Li Pan and Hou Yiyuan with dereliction, and all were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 登雲者，大學士高拱姻也。

translations.literal: Dengyun was a relative by marriage of Grand Secretary Gao Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Dengyun was related by marriage to Grand Secretary Gao Gong.

sentences.zh: 應嘉策拱必害己，遂並劾拱，言：「拱輔政初，即以直廬為隘，移家西安門外，夤夜潛歸。

translations.literal: Yingjia reckoned that Gong would surely harm him, and therefore also impeached Gong, saying: "When Gong first took up assisting government, he found the straight residence too cramped, moved his household outside Xi'an Gate, and returned secretly in the dead of night.
translations.idiomatic: Yingjia reckoned that Gao Gong would surely move against him and therefore impeached Gong as well, saying, "When Gong first took up government, he found the straight residence too cramped, moved his household outside Xi'an Gate, and slipped home in the dead of night.

sentences.zh: 陛下近稍違和，拱即私運直廬器物於外。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has recently been slightly unwell, and Gong has privately moved the furnishings of the straight residence outside.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has recently been slightly unwell, and Gong has privately moved the furnishings of the straight residence outside.

sentences.zh: 臣不知拱何心。」

translations.literal: Your subject does not know what is in Gong's heart."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject does not know what is in Gong's heart."

sentences.zh: 疏入，拱大懼，亟奏辯。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Gong was greatly afraid and urgently memorialized in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Gong was greatly afraid and urgently memorialized in his defense.

sentences.zh: 會帝崩，得不竟。

translations.literal: Just then the emperor died, and the matter was not carried through.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the emperor died, and the matter was not carried through.

sentences.zh: 拱以此銜應嘉。

translations.literal: Gong therefore bore a grudge against Yingjia.
translations.idiomatic: Gong therefore bore a grudge against Yingjia.

sentences.zh: 穆宗嗣位，應嘉請帝御文華殿與輔臣面議大政，召訪諸卿顧問侍從，令科臣隨事駁議。

translations.literal: When the Muzong emperor succeeded, Yingjia asked that the emperor preside in the Wenhua Hall to discuss great affairs face to face with chief ministers, summon and consult various ministers, advisers, and attendants, and order the supervising secretaries to debate and rebut matters as they arose.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong succeeded, Yingjia asked that the emperor preside in the Wenhua Hall to discuss great affairs face to face with chief ministers, summon ministers, advisers, and attendants for consultation, and order supervising secretaries to debate and rebut matters as they arose.

sentences.zh: 帝納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 應嘉居諫職，號敢言。

translations.literal: In his remonstrance office Yingjia was known as outspoken.
translations.idiomatic: In his remonstrance office Yingjia was known for speaking boldly.

sentences.zh: 然悻悻好搏擊，議者頗以傾危目之。

translations.literal: Yet he was resentful and fond of attack, and critics largely regarded him as one who overturned stability.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was resentful and fond of attack, and critics largely saw him as a destabilizing force.

sentences.zh: 周弘祖，麻城人。

translations.literal: Zhou Hongzu was a native of Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Hongzu came from Macheng.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十八年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 除吉安推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor of Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 征授御史，出督屯田、馬政。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed censor, and went out to supervise garrison farms and horse administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and appointed censor, then sent out to supervise garrison farms and horse administration.

sentences.zh: 隆慶改元，司禮中貴及藩邸近侍蔭錦衣指揮以下至二十余人。

translations.literal: When the Longqing reign began, eunuchs of the Directorate of Ceremonial and close attendants from the princely residence were granted hereditary posts as Embroidered Uniform Guard commanders and below, more than twenty in all.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Longqing reign, eunuchs of the Directorate of Ceremonial and close attendants from the princely residence received hereditary appointments as Embroidered Uniform Guard commanders and below—more than twenty men in all.

sentences.zh: 弘祖馳疏請止賚金幣，或停世襲，且言：「高皇帝定制，宦侍止給奔走掃除，不關政事。

translations.literal: Hongzu sent an urgent memorial asking that gold and silks not be bestowed, or that hereditary succession be halted, and further said: "The founding emperor established the system: palace attendants were only to run errands and sweep clean, with no part in government.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzu sent an urgent memorial asking that gold and silks not be bestowed, or that hereditary succession be halted, and said, "The founding emperor established the rule that palace attendants were only to run errands and sweep clean, with no part in government.

sentences.zh: 孝宗召對大臣，宦侍必退去百余武，非惟不使之預，亦且不使之聞。

translations.literal: When the Xiaozong Emperor summoned ministers for audience, palace attendants had to withdraw more than a hundred paces; they were not only kept from taking part, but even from hearing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong summoned ministers for audience, palace attendants had to withdraw more than a hundred paces—not only kept from taking part, but even from hearing.

sentences.zh: 願陛下勿與謀議，假以嚬笑，則彼無亂政之階，而聖德媲太祖、孝宗矣。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will not deliberate with them or grant them smiles and favor; then they will have no foothold to disorder government, and Your sagely virtue will match the founding emperor and Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will not deliberate with them or grant them smiles and favor; then they will have no foothold to disorder government, and Your sagely virtue will match the founding emperor and Emperor Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞先帝初載，欲蔭太監張欽義子錦衣，兵部尚書彭澤執奏再四。

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard that in the first years of the late emperor, he wished to grant hereditary Embroidered Uniform Guard rank to the adopted son of eunuch Zhang Qin, and Minister of War Peng Ze memorialized in opposition again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has also heard that in the late emperor's first years he wished to grant hereditary Embroidered Uniform Guard rank to the adopted son of eunuch Zhang Qin, and Minister of War Peng Ze memorialized in opposition again and again.

sentences.zh: 今趙炳然居澤位，不能效澤忠，無所逃罪。」

translations.literal: Now Zhao Bingran holds Ze's post yet cannot emulate Ze's loyalty; he cannot escape guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhao Bingran holds Ze's post yet cannot emulate Ze's loyalty; he cannot escape blame."

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: Acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: The court merely acknowledged receipt.

sentences.zh: 已，請汰內府監局、錦衣衛、光祿寺、文思院冗員，復嘉靖初年之舊，又請仿行古社倉制。

translations.literal: Thereafter he asked to eliminate redundant staff in the inner-palace directorates, the Embroidered Uniform Guard, the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and the Wensi Bureau, restoring the practice of the early Jiajing years, and also asked to follow the ancient communal granary system.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to cut redundant staff in the inner-palace directorates, the Embroidered Uniform Guard, the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and the Wensi Bureau, restoring early Jiajing practice, and also asked to revive the ancient communal granary system.

sentences.zh: 詔皆從之。

translations.literal: Edicts approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 明年春，言：「近四方地震，土裂成渠，旗竿數火，天鼓再鳴，隕星旋風，天雨黑豆，此皆陰盛之徵也。

translations.literal: The next spring he said: "Recently earthquakes have struck in every quarter; earth has split into channels, flagpoles have caught fire several times, the sky drum has sounded twice, meteors and whirlwinds have appeared, and black beans have rained from heaven—all signs of excessive yin.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring he said, "Lately earthquakes have struck in every quarter; earth has split into channels, flagpoles have caught fire, the sky drum has sounded twice, meteors and whirlwinds have appeared, and black beans have rained from heaven—all signs of excessive yin.

sentences.zh: 陛下嗣位二年，未嘗接見大臣，咨訪治道。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has been on the throne two years yet has never received chief ministers or consulted on the way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has been on the throne two years yet has never received chief ministers or consulted on the way of governance.

sentences.zh: 邊患孔棘，備禦無方。

translations.literal: Border troubles are acute, and there is no plan for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Border troubles are acute, and there is no plan for defense.

sentences.zh: 事涉內庭，輒見撓沮，如閱馬、核庫，詔出復停。

translations.literal: When matters touch the inner court they are at once obstructed—as with inspecting horses and auditing storehouses: edicts go out and are then halted.
translations.idiomatic: When matters touch the inner court they are at once obstructed—as with inspecting horses and auditing storehouses: edicts go out and are then halted.

sentences.zh: 皇莊則親收子粒，太和則榷取香錢，織造之使累遣，糾劾之疏留中。

translations.literal: At the imperial estates the emperor personally collects grain rents; at Mount Taihe incense money is levied; weaving envoys are sent again and again; and memorials of impeachment are held at court.
translations.idiomatic: At the imperial estates the emperor personally collects grain rents; at Mount Taihe incense money is levied; weaving envoys are sent again and again; and memorials of impeachment are held at court.

sentences.zh: 內臣爵賞謝辭，溫旨遠出六卿上，尤祖宗朝所絕無者。」

translations.literal: When inner attendants declined ennoblement and rewards, warm edicts placed them far above the six ministers—something utterly unknown in the reigns of the dynastic founders."
translations.idiomatic: When inner attendants declined ennoblement and rewards, warm edicts placed them far above the six ministers—something utterly unknown under the dynastic founders."

sentences.zh: 疏入，不報。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, no response was given.

sentences.zh: 其冬詔市珍寶，魏時亮等爭，不聽。

translations.literal: That winter an edict ordered the purchase of precious objects; Wei Shiliang and others protested, but were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: That winter an edict ordered the purchase of precious objects; Wei Shiliang and others protested, but were not heeded.

sentences.zh: 弘祖復切諫。

translations.literal: Hongzu again remonstrated forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzu remonstrated again in strong terms.

sentences.zh: 尋遷福建提學副使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Educational Vice Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Educational Vice Commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 大學士高拱掌吏部，考察言官，惡弘祖及岑用賓等，謫弘祖安順判官，用賓宜川縣丞。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Gao Gong headed the Ministry of Personnel, reviewed the remonstrance officials, hated Hongzu and Cen Yongbin and others, and demoted Hongzu to judge of Anshun and Yongbin to county assistant of Yichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Gao Gong headed the Ministry of Personnel, reviewed the remonstrance officials, hated Hongzu and Cen Yongbin and others, and demoted Hongzu to judge of Anshun and Yongbin to county assistant of Yichuan.

sentences.zh: 用賓，廣東順德人。

translations.literal: Yongbin was a native of Shunde in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Yongbin came from Shunde in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 官南京給事中，多所論劾。

translations.literal: He served as supervising secretary in Nanjing and impeached many.
translations.idiomatic: As supervising secretary in Nanjing he impeached many officials.

sentences.zh: 又嘗論拱很愎，以故拱憾之，出為紹興知府。

translations.literal: He had also once criticized Gong as obstinate and willful; for this Gong resented him and sent him out as prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: He had also criticized Gao Gong as obstinate and willful; for this Gong resented him and sent him out as prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 既中以察典，遂卒於貶所。

translations.literal: He was soon caught in the personnel review and died in his place of demotion.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon caught in the personnel review and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 而弘祖謫未幾，拱罷，量移廣平推官，萬歷中，屢遷南京光祿卿。

translations.literal: Hongzu had not long been demoted when Gong was dismissed; he was transferred in grade to investigating censor of Guangping, and in the Wanli years was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzu had not long been demoted when Gao Gong fell; he was transferred in grade to investigating censor of Guangping, and in the Wanli years rose repeatedly to Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 坐朱衣謁陵免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for wearing vermilion robes when paying respects at the mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for wearing vermilion robes when paying respects at the imperial mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 當隆慶初，以地震言事者，又有鄧洪震，宣化人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, among those who spoke on affairs because of earthquakes was also Deng Hongzhen, a native of Xuanhua.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing, among those who spoke out after earthquakes was Deng Hongzhen, who came from Xuanhua.

sentences.zh: 時為兵部郎中，上疏曰：「入夏以來，淫雨彌月。

translations.literal: At the time he was a bureau director in the Ministry of War and submitted a memorial saying: "Since summer began, excessive rain has lasted a full month.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he was a bureau director in the Ministry of War and memorialized, "Since summer began, excessive rain has lasted a full month.

sentences.zh: 又京師去冬地震，今春風霾大作，白日無光。

translations.literal: Last winter the capital region suffered earthquake; this spring dust storms have raged and the sun has been without light.
translations.idiomatic: Last winter the capital region suffered an earthquake; this spring dust storms have raged and the sun has been dimmed.

sentences.zh: 近大同又報雨雹傷物，地震有聲。

translations.literal: Recently Datong has also reported hail damaging crops and an earthquake with sound.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Datong has also reported hail damaging crops and an earthquake that was heard.

sentences.zh: 陛下臨禦甫半年，災異疊見。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has held court barely half a year, yet calamities and prodigies have appeared one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has held court barely half a year, yet calamities and prodigies have appeared one after another.

sentences.zh: 傳聞後宮遊幸無時，嬪禦相隨，後車充斥。

translations.literal: It is rumored that the inner palace goes out at all hours without schedule, with consorts and attendants following and the rear carriages packed full.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor says the inner palace goes out at all hours without schedule, with consorts and attendants following and the rear carriages packed full.

sentences.zh: 左右近習，濫賜予。

translations.literal: Close attendants receive lavish gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Close attendants receive lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 政令屢易，前後背馳，邪正混淆，用舍猶豫。

translations.literal: Government orders change repeatedly, contradicting one another; the wicked and upright are confused, and appointments and dismissals are hesitant.
translations.idiomatic: Government orders change repeatedly and contradict one another; the wicked and upright are confused, and appointments and dismissals are hesitant.

sentences.zh: 萬一奸宄潛生，寇戎軼犯，其何以待之？」

translations.literal: If by chance treachery arises in secret or border raiders strike suddenly, how will you meet it?"
translations.idiomatic: If treachery arises in secret or border raiders strike suddenly, how will you meet it?"

sentences.zh: 帝納其言，下禮官議修省。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words and ordered the ritual officials to deliberate on self-reform.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his words and ordered the ritual officials to deliberate on self-reform.

sentences.zh: 洪震尋以疾歸。

translations.literal: Hongzhen soon returned home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhen soon returned home on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 萬歷改元，督撫交章論薦，竟不起。

translations.literal: When the Wanli reign began, regional commanders and grand coordinators submitted memorials recommending him one after another, but in the end he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wanli reign began, regional commanders and grand coordinators recommended him in memorial after memorial, but in the end he did not take office.

sentences.zh: 詹仰庇，字汝欽，安溪人。

translations.literal: Zhan Yangbi, style Ruqin, was a native of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Yangbi, styled Ruqin, came from Anxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-fourth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 由南海知縣征授御史。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Nanhai he was summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: From magistrate of Nanhai he was summoned and appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，穆宗詔戶部購寶珠，尚書馬森執奏，給事中魏時亮、御史賀一桂等繼爭，皆不聽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, the Muzong emperor ordered the Ministry of Revenue to purchase precious pearls; Minister Ma Sen memorialized in opposition, and Supervising Secretary Wei Shiliang, Censor He Yigui, and others protested in turn, but none were heeded.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing, Emperor Muzong ordered the Ministry of Revenue to purchase precious pearls; Minister Ma Sen memorialized in opposition, and Supervising Secretary Wei Shiliang, Censor He Yigui, and others protested in turn, but none were heeded.

sentences.zh: 仰庇疏言：「頃言官諫購寶珠，反蒙詰讓。

translations.literal: Yangbi memorialized: "Just now remonstrance officials advised against purchasing pearls and were rebuked instead.
translations.idiomatic: Yangbi memorialized, "Just now remonstrance officials advised against purchasing pearls and were rebuked instead.

sentences.zh: 昔仲虺戒湯不邇聲色，不殖貨利；

translations.literal: In old times Zhong Hui admonished Tang not to draw near sounds and colors or amass goods for profit;
translations.idiomatic: In old times Zhong Hui admonished Tang not to draw near sounds and colors or amass goods for profit;

sentences.zh: 召公戒武王玩人喪德，玩物喪誌。

translations.literal: the Duke of Shao admonished King Wu that to toy with men is to lose virtue, and to toy with things is to lose purpose.
translations.idiomatic: the Duke of Shao admonished King Wu that to toy with men is to lose virtue, and to toy with things is to lose purpose.

sentences.zh: 湯、武能受二臣之戒，絕去玩好，故聖德光千載。

translations.literal: Tang and Wu were able to accept the admonitions of these two ministers and cut off indulgence in playthings and delights; therefore their sagely virtue shines for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Tang and Wu accepted the admonitions of these two ministers and cut off indulgence in playthings and delights; therefore their sagely virtue shines for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 若侈心一生，不可復遏，恣情縱欲，財耗民窮。

translations.literal: Once the heart of extravagance is born it cannot be checked again; to indulge feeling and release desire exhausts wealth and impoverishes the people.
translations.idiomatic: Once the heart of extravagance is born it cannot be checked again; to indulge feeling and release desire exhausts wealth and impoverishes the people.

sentences.zh: 陛下玩好之端漸啟，弼違之諫惡聞，群小乘隙，百方誘惑，害有不勝言者。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's indulgence in delights has gradually opened; admonitions that oppose you are hated to hear; the multitude of petty men seize their openings and tempt from every side—harms beyond numbering.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's indulgence in delights has gradually opened; admonitions that oppose you are hated to hear; petty men seize their openings and tempt from every side—harms beyond numbering.

sentences.zh: 況寶石珠璣，多藏中貴家，求之愈急，邀直愈多，奈何以有用財，耗之無用之物。

translations.literal: Moreover gems and pearls are mostly hoarded in eunuch households; the more urgently they are sought, the more bribes are demanded—how can useful funds be squandered on useless things?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover gems and pearls are mostly hoarded in eunuch households; the more urgently they are sought, the more bribes are demanded—how can useful funds be squandered on useless things?

sentences.zh: 今兩廣需餉，疏請再三，猶靳不予，何輕重倒置乎！」

translations.literal: Now the two Guang regions need pay; memorials have requested it again and again, yet it is still withheld—how is priority turned upside down!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the two Guang regions need military pay; memorials have requested it again and again, yet it is still withheld—how is priority turned upside down!"

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: No response was given.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，中官制煙火，延燒禁中廬舍，仰庇請按治。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, eunuchs made fireworks that spread and burned lodges within the forbidden precinct; Yangbi asked that they be investigated and punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, eunuchs made fireworks that spread and burned lodges within the forbidden precinct; Yangbi asked that they be investigated and punished.

sentences.zh: 左右近習多切齒者。

translations.literal: Many close attendants gnashed their teeth at him.
translations.idiomatic: Many close attendants gnashed their teeth at him.

sentences.zh: 帝頗耽聲色，陳皇后微諫，帝怒，出之別宮。

translations.literal: The emperor was rather addicted to sounds and colors; Empress Chen remonstrated mildly, and the emperor in anger sent her to a separate palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was rather addicted to sounds and colors; Empress Chen remonstrated mildly, and the emperor in anger sent her to a separate palace.

sentences.zh: 外庭皆憂之，莫敢言。

translations.literal: The outer court was all anxious, but none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: The outer court was anxious, but none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 仰庇入朝，遇醫禁中出。

translations.literal: Yangbi entered court and met a physician coming out of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yangbi entered court and met a physician coming out of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 詢之，知後寢疾危篤，即上疏言：「先帝慎擇賢淑，作配陛下，為宗廟社稷內主。

translations.literal: Inquiring, he learned that the empress lay gravely ill in her chamber, and at once submitted a memorial saying: "The late emperor carefully chose a worthy and virtuous consort to be Your Majesty's mate, the inner mistress of the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: On inquiry he learned that the empress lay gravely ill, and at once memorialized, "The late emperor carefully chose a worthy and virtuous consort to be Your Majesty's mate, the inner mistress of the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜遵先帝命，篤宮闈之好。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should follow the late emperor's command and deepen the affection of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should follow the late emperor's command and deepen the affection of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 近聞皇后移居別宮，已近一載，抑郁成疾，陛下略不省視。

translations.literal: Recently it is heard that the empress was moved to a separate palace nearly a year ago, fell ill from depression, and Your Majesty has scarcely visited her.
translations.idiomatic: Recently it is heard that the empress was moved to a separate palace nearly a year ago, fell ill from depression, and Your Majesty has scarcely visited her.

sentences.zh: 萬一不諱，如聖德何？

translations.literal: If by chance the worst should happen, what of Your sagely virtue?
translations.idiomatic: If the worst should happen, what of Your sagely virtue?

sentences.zh: 臣下莫不憂惶，徒以事涉宮禁，不敢頌言。

translations.literal: Your subjects are all anxious and fearful, yet because the matter touches the forbidden palace they dare not speak openly.
translations.idiomatic: Your subjects are all anxious and fearful, yet because the matter touches the forbidden palace they dare not speak openly.

sentences.zh: 臣謂人臣之義，知而不言，當死；

translations.literal: Your subject holds that the duty of a minister is: to know and not speak deserves death;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject holds that a minister who knows and does not speak deserves death;

sentences.zh: 言而觸諱，亦當死。

translations.literal: to speak and touch taboo also deserves death.
translations.idiomatic: to speak and touch taboo also deserves death.

sentences.zh: 臣今日固不惜死，願陛下采聽臣言，立復皇后中宮，時加慰問，臣雖死賢於生。」

translations.literal: Your subject today truly does not spare his life; I pray Your Majesty will heed my words, immediately restore the empress to the central palace, and visit her from time to time with comfort—then though I die I am better off than living."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject today truly does not spare his life; I pray Your Majesty will heed my words, immediately restore the empress to the central palace, and visit her from time to time with comfort—then though I die I am better off than living."

sentences.zh: 帝手批答曰：「後無子多病，移居別宮，聊自適，以冀卻疾。

translations.literal: The emperor wrote a reply in his own hand: "The empress is childless and often ill; she was moved to a separate palace merely to suit herself, in hope of recovering.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote a reply in his own hand: "The empress is childless and often ill; she was moved to a separate palace merely to suit herself, in hope of recovering.

sentences.zh: 爾何知內庭事，顧妄言。」

translations.literal: What do you know of inner-court affairs, that you speak rashly?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you know of inner-court affairs, that you speak rashly?"

sentences.zh: 仰庇自分得重譴，同列亦危之。

translations.literal: Yangbi himself expected heavy punishment, and his colleagues also feared for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yangbi himself expected heavy punishment, and his colleagues also feared for him.

sentences.zh: 及旨下，中外驚喜過望，仰庇益感奮。

translations.literal: When the edict came down, inside and outside the court were astonished beyond expectation, and Yangbi was all the more stirred.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict came down, inside and outside the court were astonished beyond expectation, and Yangbi was all the more stirred.

sentences.zh: 亡何，巡視十庫，疏言：「內官監歲入租稅至多，而歲出不置籍。

translations.literal: Before long, inspecting the ten storehouses, he memorialized: "The Directorate of Palace Attendants receives the most rent and tax each year, yet yearly expenditures are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, inspecting the ten storehouses, he memorialized, "The Directorate of Palace Attendants receives the most rent and tax each year, yet yearly expenditures are not recorded.

sentences.zh: 按京城內外園廛場地，隸本監者數十計，歲課皆屬官錢，而內臣假上供名，恣意漁獵。

translations.literal: According to gardens, markets, and grounds inside and outside the capital under this directorate, they number several tens; yearly levies all belong to official funds, yet inner attendants under the name of tribute to the throne fish and hunt as they please.
translations.idiomatic: Gardens, markets, and grounds inside and outside the capital under this directorate number several tens; yearly levies all belong to official funds, yet inner attendants under the name of tribute to the throne extort as they please.

sentences.zh: 利填私家，過歸朝寧。

translations.literal: Profit fills private homes while excess returns to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Profit fills private homes while excess returns to the court.

sentences.zh: 乞備核宜留宜革，並出入多寡數，以杜奸欺。

translations.literal: I beg a full audit of what should be kept and what abolished, together with the amounts of income and outgo, to stop fraud.
translations.idiomatic: I beg a full audit of what should be kept and what abolished, together with the amounts of income and outgo, to stop fraud.

sentences.zh: 再照人主奢儉，四方系安危。

translations.literal: Again, the ruler's extravagance or frugality bears on the safety or peril of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the ruler's extravagance or frugality bears on the safety or peril of the realm.

sentences.zh: 陛下前取戶部銀，用備緩急。

translations.literal: Your Majesty earlier took silver from the Ministry of Revenue to meet emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty earlier took silver from the Ministry of Revenue to meet emergencies.

sentences.zh: 今如本監所稱，則盡以創鰲山、修宮苑、制鞦韆、造龍鳳艦、治金櫃玉盆。

translations.literal: Now, as this directorate reports, it has all been spent on building the Tortoise Mountain, repairing palace gardens, making swings, constructing dragon-phoenix ships, and making gold cabinets and jade basins.
translations.idiomatic: Now, as this directorate reports, it has all been spent on building the Tortoise Mountain, repairing palace gardens, making swings, constructing dragon-phoenix ships, and making gold cabinets and jade basins.

sentences.zh: 群小因幹沒，累聖德，虧國計。

translations.literal: Petty men thereby embezzle, burdening sagely virtue and harming the state plan.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men thereby embezzle, burdening sagely virtue and harming the state treasury.

sentences.zh: 望陛下深省，有以玩好逢迎者，悉屏出罪之。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will reflect deeply and dismiss and punish all who use delights to curry favor."
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will reflect deeply and dismiss and punish all who use delights to curry favor."

sentences.zh: 宦官益恨。

translations.literal: The eunuchs hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs hated him all the more.

sentences.zh: 故事，諸司文移往還及牧民官出教，用「照」字，言官上書無此體。

translations.literal: By precedent, when offices exchanged documents and local officials issued instructions, they used the character "zhao"; remonstrance officials' memorials had no such form.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when offices exchanged documents and local officials issued instructions, they used the character "zhao"; remonstrance officials' memorials had no such form.

sentences.zh: 宦官因指「再照人主」語，為大不敬。

translations.literal: The eunuchs therefore seized on the phrase "again, the ruler" as gross disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs therefore seized on the phrase "again, the ruler" as gross disrespect.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下詔曰：「仰庇小臣，敢照及天子，且狂肆屢不悛。」

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and issued an edict: "Yangbi is a petty official who dares use zhao toward the Son of Heaven, and is moreover wild and unrestrained, repeatedly unrepentant."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and issued an edict: "Yangbi is a petty official who dares use zhao toward the Son of Heaven, and is moreover wild and unrestrained, repeatedly unrepentant."

sentences.zh: 遂廷杖百，除名，並罷科道之巡視庫藏者。

translations.literal: He was then beaten a hundred strokes at court, dismissed from the rolls, and the censorate officials inspecting the storehouses were also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was then beaten a hundred strokes at court, dismissed from the rolls, and the censorate officials inspecting the storehouses were also dismissed.

sentences.zh: 南京給事中駱問禮、御史余嘉詔等疏救，且言巡視官不當罷。

translations.literal: Nanjing Supervising Secretary Luo Wenli, Censor Yu Jiazhao, and others memorialized in his defense, and said the inspection officials should not be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing Supervising Secretary Luo Wenli, Censor Yu Jiazhao, and others memorialized in his defense and said the inspection officials should not be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: This was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: This was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 仰庇為御史僅八月，數進讜言，竟以獲罪。

translations.literal: Yangbi had been censor only eight months, offered forthright counsel several times, and in the end was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Yangbi had been censor only eight months, offered forthright counsel several times, and in the end was punished.

sentences.zh: 神宗嗣位，錄先朝直臣。

translations.literal: When the Shenzong emperor succeeded, he recorded the upright ministers of the previous reign.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong succeeded, he recorded the upright ministers of the previous reign.

sentences.zh: 以仰庇在京時嘗為商人居間，不得內召，除廣東參議。

translations.literal: Because while in the capital Yangbi had once acted as go-between for merchants, he was not summoned within; he was appointed administration commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Because while in the capital Yangbi had once acted as go-between for merchants, he was not summoned within; he was appointed administration commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 尋乞歸。

translations.literal: Soon he asked to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to return home.

sentences.zh: 家居十餘年，起官江西。

translations.literal: He lived at home more than ten years, then was raised to office in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home more than ten years, then was raised to office in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 再遷南京太僕少卿。

translations.literal: After two transfers he became Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After two transfers he became Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 入為左僉都御史，進左副都御史。

translations.literal: He entered court as Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief and advanced to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief and advanced to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 仰庇初以直節負盛名，至是為保位計，頗不免附麗。

translations.literal: Yangbi had first been famed for upright integrity, but by now, calculating to preserve his position, he could not altogether avoid clinging to powerful patrons.
translations.idiomatic: Yangbi had first been famed for upright integrity, but by now, calculating to preserve his position, he could not altogether avoid clinging to powerful patrons.

sentences.zh: 饒伸以科場事劾大學士王錫爵、左都御史吳時來，仰庇即劾伸。

translations.literal: Rao Shen impeached Grand Secretary Wang Xijue and Left Censor-in-Chief Wu Shilai over the examination-field affair; Yangbi at once impeached Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Rao Shen impeached Grand Secretary Wang Xijue and Left Censor-in-Chief Wu Shilai over the examination-field affair; Yangbi at once impeached Shen.

sentences.zh: 進士薛敷教劾時來及南京右都御史耿定向，仰庇未及閱疏，即論敷教排陷大臣，敷教坐廢。

translations.literal: Jinshi Xue Fujiao impeached Shilai and Nanjing Right Censor-in-Chief Geng Dingxiang; Yangbi had not yet read the memorial when he charged that Fujiao was framing great ministers, and Fujiao was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi Xue Fujiao impeached Shilai and Nanjing Right Censor-in-Chief Geng Dingxiang; Yangbi had not yet read the memorial when he charged that Fujiao was framing great ministers, and Fujiao was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 及吏部侍郎趙煥、兵部侍郎沈子木相繼去，仰庇謀代之，蹤跡頗著。

translations.literal: When Vice Minister of Personnel Zhao Huan and Vice Minister of War Shen Zimu left office in succession, Yangbi plotted to replace them, and his tracks were rather plain.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Minister of Personnel Zhao Huan and Vice Minister of War Shen Zimu left office in succession, Yangbi plotted to replace them, and his tracks were rather plain.

sentences.zh: 給事中王繼光、主事姜延士昌、員外郎趙南星、南京御史王麟趾等交章論列。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wang Jiguang, Section Director Jiang Yan, Bureau Director Zhao Nanxing, Nanjing Censor Wang Linzhi, and others submitted memorials one after another discussing him.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Wang Jiguang, Section Director Jiang Yan, Bureau Director Zhao Nanxing, Nanjing Censor Wang Linzhi, and others submitted memorial after memorial discussing him.

sentences.zh: 仰庇不自安，屢求去。

translations.literal: Yangbi was ill at ease and repeatedly asked to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Yangbi was ill at ease and repeatedly asked to leave.

sentences.zh: 帝雖慰留，而眾議籍籍不止。

translations.literal: Although the emperor comforted him and kept him, public discussion buzzed unceasingly.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor comforted him and urged him to stay, public criticism never ceased.

sentences.zh: 稍遷刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to Right Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 移疾歸，久之卒。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and returned home; after a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and retired; after some time he died.

sentences.zh: 駱問禮，諸暨人。

translations.literal: Luo Wenli was a native of Zhuji.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Wenli was a native of Zhuji.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖末進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the late Jiajing reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the late Jiajing era.

sentences.zh: 歷南京刑科給事中。

translations.literal: He served as supervising secretary of the Penalties Section in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a supervising secretary in the Penalties Section at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年，陳皇后移別宮，問禮偕同官張應治等上言：「皇后正位中闈，即有疾，豈宜移宮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longqing, when Empress Chen was moved to a separate palace, Wenli together with his colleague Zhang Yingzhi and others submitted a memorial: "The empress holds her proper place in the inner quarters; even if she is ill, how is it fitting to move her palace?
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 3, when Empress Chen was moved to another palace, Wenli and his colleague Zhang Yingzhi and others memorialized: "The empress holds her rightful place in the inner quarters; even if she is ill, how can she be moved from her palace?

sentences.zh: 望亟返坤寧，毋使後世謂變禮自陛下始。」

translations.literal: We hope she will speedily return to Kunning Palace, lest posterity say that altering ritual began with Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: We pray she be brought back to Kunning Palace at once, lest posterity say that ritual was first altered under Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: No response was given.

sentences.zh: 給事張齊劾徐階，為廷臣所排，下獄削籍。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhang Qi impeached Xu Jie, was repulsed by court ministers, imprisoned, and stripped from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhang Qi impeached Xu Jie, was ostracized by court ministers, imprisoned, and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 問禮獨言齊贓可疑，不當以糾彈大臣實其罪。

translations.literal: Wenli alone said Qi's bribery was suspicious and that one should not establish his guilt by having him impeach great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Wenli alone argued that Qi's bribery charges were dubious and that his guilt should not be established simply because he had impeached senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 張居正請大閱，問禮謂非要務，而請帝日親萬幾，詳覽奏章。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng requested a grand review; Wenli said it was not an urgent task and asked the emperor to personally handle the myriad affairs of state daily and read memorials in detail.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng requested a grand military review, Wenli said it was not the urgent priority and urged the emperor to attend daily to state affairs and review memorials carefully.

sentences.zh: 未幾，劾誠意伯劉世延、福建巡撫塗澤民不職，帝並留之。

translations.literal: Before long he impeached Marquis of Chengyi Liu Shiyan and Fujian Grand Coordinator Tu Zemin for malfeasance; the emperor kept both in office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he impeached Marquis of Chengyi Liu Shiyan and Fujian Grand Coordinator Tu Zemin for incompetence; the emperor retained both men.

sentences.zh: 帝初納言官請，將令諸政務悉面奏於便殿，問禮遂條上面奏事宜。

translations.literal: When the emperor at first accepted the remonstrance officials' request and was about to have all government business reported face-to-face in the informal hall, Wenli thereupon itemized points on the face-to-face audience.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first accepted the remonstrance officials' request and proposed that all government business be presented face-to-face in the informal hall, Wenli submitted a detailed memorial on how such audiences should be conducted.

sentences.zh: 一言：「陛下躬攬萬幾，宜酌用群言，不執己見，使可否予奪，皆合天道，則有獨斷之美，無自用之失。」

translations.literal: First point: "Your Majesty personally handles the myriad affairs of state; you should weigh and use the counsel of the multitude, not cling to your own views, so that approvals and denials all accord with Heaven's Way—then you will have the virtue of decisive judgment without the error of self-will."
translations.idiomatic: First point: "Your Majesty personally handles the myriad affairs of state; you should weigh the counsel of many voices rather than cling to your own views, so that every approval and denial accords with Heaven's Way—then you will have the virtue of decisive judgment without the error of acting on whim alone."

sentences.zh: 二言：「陛下宜日居便殿，使侍從官常在左右，非向晦不入宮闈，則涵養薰陶，自多裨益。」

translations.literal: Second point: "Your Majesty should daily stay in the informal hall and keep attendant officials constantly at your side, not entering the inner palace except when dusk approaches—then moral cultivation will bring much benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Second point: "Your Majesty should remain daily in the informal hall with attendant officials always at hand, entering the inner palace only as dusk approaches—then steady moral cultivation will bring great benefit."

sentences.zh: 三言：「內閣政事根本，宜參用諸司，無拘翰林，則講明義理，通達政事，皆得其人。」

translations.literal: Third point: "The Grand Secretariat is the root of government; ministers should be drawn from all bureaus without restricting selection to the Hanlin Academy—then those who expound principle and those who understand affairs will each be properly chosen."
translations.idiomatic: Third point: "The Grand Secretariat is the foundation of government; ministers should be drawn from all bureaus without limiting selection to the Hanlin Academy—then those who expound principle and those who understand affairs will each be properly placed."

sentences.zh: 四言「詔旨必由六科，諸司始得奉行，脫有未當，許封還執奏。

translations.literal: Fourth point: "Edicts must pass through the Six Sections before bureaus may carry them out; if anything is improper, allow them to return the sealed memorial and remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth point: "Edicts must pass through the Six Sections before bureaus may carry them out; if anything is improper, allow them to return the sealed memorial and remonstrate in person.

sentences.zh: 如六科不封駁，諸司失檢察者，許御史糾彈。」

translations.literal: If the Six Sections do not seal and return objections, and bureaus fail in oversight, allow censors to impeach."
translations.idiomatic: If the Six Sections fail to seal and return objections, and bureaus neglect their oversight, censors should be allowed to impeach."

sentences.zh: 五言：「頃詔書兩下，皆許諸人直言。

translations.literal: Fifth point: "Recently two edicts were issued, both allowing all to speak frankly.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth point: "Recently two edicts were issued, both allowing everyone to speak frankly.

sentences.zh: 然所采納者，除言官與一二大臣外，盡付所司而已。

translations.literal: Yet what was adopted, apart from remonstrance officials and one or two great ministers, was simply handed over to the relevant bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what was adopted, apart from remonstrance officials and one or two senior ministers, was simply handed over to the relevant bureaus.

sentences.zh: 宜益廣言路，凡臣民章奏，不惟其人惟其言，令匹夫皆得自效。」

translations.literal: You should further broaden the avenue of speech: for all memorials from ministers and commoners, judge not the person but the words, so that even common men may offer themselves."
translations.idiomatic: You should further broaden the avenue of remonstrance: for all memorials from ministers and commoners, judge not the person but the words, so that even common men may serve the state."

sentences.zh: 六言：「陛下臨朝決事，凡給事左右，如傳旨、接奏章之類，宜用文武侍從，毋使中官參與，則窺竊之漸，無自而生。」

translations.literal: Sixth point: "When Your Majesty decides affairs at court, all attendant duties—such as transmitting edicts and receiving memorials—should use civil and military attendants; do not let eunuchs participate, and the first steps toward usurpation will never arise."
translations.idiomatic: Sixth point: "When Your Majesty decides affairs at court, all attendant duties—such as transmitting edicts and receiving memorials—should be entrusted to civil and military attendants; do not let eunuchs take part, and the first steps toward usurpation will never arise."

sentences.zh: 七言：「士習傾危，稍或異同，輒加排陷。

translations.literal: Seventh point: "Scholarly custom has turned perilous: the slightest difference brings attack and framing.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh point: "Scholarly custom has grown perilous: the slightest difference of opinion brings attack and framing.

sentences.zh: 自今凡議國事，惟論是非，不徇好惡。

translations.literal: From now on, in all discussion of state affairs, judge only right and wrong, not personal likes and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, in all discussion of state affairs, judge only right and wrong, not personal likes and dislikes.

sentences.zh: 眾人言未必得，一人言未必非，則公論日明，士氣可振。」

translations.literal: What many say is not necessarily right, and what one says is not necessarily wrong—then public judgment will daily grow clearer and scholarly morale can be revived."
translations.idiomatic: What many say is not necessarily right, and what one says is not necessarily wrong—then public judgment will daily grow clearer and scholarly morale can be revived."

sentences.zh: 八言：「政令之出，宜在必行。

translations.literal: Eighth point: "When orders issue forth, they should be enforced without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth point: "When orders issue forth, they should be enforced without fail.

sentences.zh: 今所司題覆，已報可者未見修舉，因循玩愒，習為故常。

translations.literal: Today in bureau replies, items already approved are not implemented; procrastination and negligence have become routine.
translations.idiomatic: Today in bureau replies, items already approved are never carried out; procrastination and negligence have become routine.

sentences.zh: 陛下當明作於上，敕諸臣奮勵於下，以挽頹惰之風」。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should give clear direction above and charge ministers below to exert themselves, to reverse the tide of decay and indolence."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should give clear direction above and charge ministers below to exert themselves, to reverse the tide of decay and indolence."

sentences.zh: 九言：「面奏之儀，宜略去繁文，務求實用，俾諸臣入而敷奏，退而治事，無或兩妨，斯上下之交可久。」

translations.literal: Ninth point: "The ritual of face-to-face audience should strip away needless formality and seek practical use, so ministers may enter to report, withdraw to govern, with neither duty hindering the other—then exchange between above and below can endure."
translations.idiomatic: Ninth point: "The ritual of face-to-face audience should strip away needless formality and seek practical use, so ministers may enter to report and withdraw to govern without either duty hindering the other—then relations between ruler and ministers can endure."

sentences.zh: 十言：「修撰、編檢諸臣，宜令更番入直，密邇乘輿，一切言動，執簡侍書。

translations.literal: Tenth point: "Drafting and editing compilers should rotate into attendance close to the imperial carriage, recording all words and deeds with brush in hand.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth point: "Drafting and editing compilers should rotate into attendance close to the imperial carriage, recording every word and deed with brush in hand.

sentences.zh: 其耳目所不及者，諸司或以月報，或以季報，令得隨事纂緝，以垂勸戒。」

translations.literal: Matters beyond their sight and hearing, bureaus might report monthly or quarterly, allowing compilation as events occur to serve as warning and instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Matters beyond their sight and hearing, bureaus might report monthly or quarterly, allowing events to be compiled as they occur to serve as warning and instruction."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝不悅。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 宦侍復從中構之，謫楚雄知事。

translations.literal: Eunuch attendants again slandered him from within; he was demoted to bureau official at Chuxiong.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch attendants again slandered him from within, and he was demoted to bureau official at Chuxiong.

sentences.zh: 明年，吏部舉雜職官當遷者，問禮及御史楊松在舉中。

translations.literal: The next year, when the Ministry of Personnel listed miscellaneous officials due for promotion, Wenli and Censor Yang Song were on the list.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the Ministry of Personnel listed miscellaneous officials due for promotion, Wenli and Censor Yang Song were on the list.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此兩人安得遽遷，俟三年後議之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How can these two men be promoted so soon? Let it be considered after three years."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "How can these two men be promoted so soon? Let it be considered after three years."

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，屢遷湖廣副使，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Commissioner of Huguang, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wanli reign he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Commissioner of Huguang, and died.

sentences.zh: 楊松，河南衛人。

translations.literal: Yang Song was a native of Henan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Song was a native of Henan Guard.

sentences.zh: 歷官御史，巡視皇城。

translations.literal: He served as censor and inspected the Imperial City.
translations.idiomatic: He served as censor and inspected the Imperial City.

sentences.zh: 尚膳少監黃雄征子錢與民哄，兵馬司捕送松所。

translations.literal: Assistant Director of the Imperial Pantry Huang Xiong lent money at interest and brawled with commoners; the Horse and Circuit Office arrested him and sent him to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Director of the Imperial Pantry Huang Xiong lent money at usurious rates and brawled with commoners; the Horse and Circuit Office arrested him and brought him before Song.

sentences.zh: 事未決，而內監令校尉趣雄入直，詭言有駕帖。

translations.literal: Before the matter was decided, an inner eunuch sent guards to hurry Xiong to palace duty, falsely claiming there was an imperial summons.
translations.idiomatic: Before the matter was decided, an inner eunuch sent guards to hurry Xiong to palace duty, falsely claiming there was an imperial summons.

sentences.zh: 松驗問無有，遂劾雄詐稱詔旨。

translations.literal: Song examined and questioned and found none; he then impeached Xiong for falsely claiming an imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Song investigated and found no such summons; he then impeached Xiong for falsely claiming an imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 帝令黜兵馬司官，而鐫松三秩，謫山西布政司照磨。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Horse and Circuit Office officials dismissed, but reduced Song three ranks and demoted him to registrar of the Shanxi Provincial Administration Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Horse and Circuit Office officials dismissed, but reduced Song three ranks and demoted him to registrar of the Shanxi Provincial Administration Commission.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，擢廬州推官，終山西副使。

translations.literal: When Shenzong acceded, he was promoted to magistrate of Luzhou and ended as Vice Commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong acceded, he was promoted to magistrate of Luzhou and ended his career as Vice Commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 張應治，秀水人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yingzhi was a native of Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yingzhi was a native of Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 在垣中抗疏，多可稱。

translations.literal: While in the censorate he submitted bold memorials, many of them praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: While in the censorate he submitted bold memorials, many of them praiseworthy.

sentences.zh: 為高拱所惡，出為九江知府。

translations.literal: He was hated by Gao Gong and was sent out as prefect of Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong took a dislike to him, and he was sent out as prefect of Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 終山東副使。

translations.literal: He ended as Vice Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Vice Commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 鄭履淳，字叔初，刑部尚書曉子也。

translations.literal: Zheng Luchun, style Shuchu, was the son of Minister of Justice Zheng Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Luchun, style Shuchu, was the son of Minister of Justice Zheng Xiao.

sentences.zh: 舉嘉靖四十年進士，除刑部主事，遷尚寶丞。
