translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fortieth year of Jiajing, was appointed section director in the Ministry of Justice, and was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Jiajing 40, was appointed section director in the Ministry of Justice, and was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年冬，疏言：

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Longqing, he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Longqing 3, he submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 頃年以來，萬民失業，四方多故，天鳴地震，災害洊臻，正陛下宵旰憂勤時也。

translations.literal: In recent years the myriad people have lost their livelihoods, troubles multiply on all sides, heaven sounds and earth quakes, disasters come in succession—this is precisely when Your Majesty should toil through the night with concern.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the people have lost their livelihoods, troubles multiply on every side, heaven sounds and earth quakes, and disasters come one after another—this is precisely when Your Majesty should toil through the night with concern.

sentences.zh: 夫饑寒迫身，易為衣食，嗷嗷赤子，聖主之所以為資。

translations.literal: When hunger and cold press upon the body, one easily turns to food and clothing; the wailing infants are the very resource upon which a sage ruler relies.
translations.idiomatic: When hunger and cold press upon the body, people easily turn to food and clothing alone; the wailing infants are the very resource upon which a sage ruler relies.

sentences.zh: 不及今定周家桑土之謀，切虞廷困窮之懼，則上天所以警動海內者，適足以資他人矣。

translations.literal: If you do not now settle the plan of the Zhou for mulberry lands and soil, but deeply fear the poverty of the court of Yu, then what heaven uses to warn and stir the realm will only supply others.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not now settle the plan of the Zhou for mulberry lands and soil, but deeply fear the poverty of the court of Yu, then what heaven uses to warn and stir the realm will only supply your enemies.

sentences.zh: 今最急莫如用賢。

translations.literal: Today nothing is more urgent than employing the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Today nothing is more urgent than employing the worthy.

sentences.zh: 陛下禦極三祀矣，曾召問一大臣，面質一講官，賞納一諫士，以共畫思患豫防之策乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty has held the throne three years—have you ever summoned a great minister to inquire, face-to-face examined a lecturer, rewarded and accepted one remonstrating scholar, to jointly devise policies for thinking ahead to dangers and taking preventive measures?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has held the throne three years—have you ever summoned a senior minister to inquire of him, face-to-face examined a lecturer, or rewarded and accepted one remonstrating scholar, to jointly devise policies for thinking ahead to dangers and taking preventive measures?

sentences.zh: 高亢暌孤，乾坤否隔，忠言重折檻之罰，儒臣虛納牖之功，宮闈違脫珥之規，朝陛拂同舟之義。

translations.literal: Lofty and aloof, heaven and earth blocked in separation, loyal words repeatedly meet with the punishment of breaking the balustrade, Confucian ministers vainly perform the service of offering counsel through the window, the inner palace violates the rule of removing earrings to remonstrate, and the court steps violate the spirit of sharing one boat.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty and aloof, heaven and earth blocked in separation, loyal words repeatedly meet with the punishment of breaking the balustrade, Confucian ministers vainly perform the service of offering counsel through the window, the inner palace violates the rule of removing earrings to remonstrate, and the court steps violate the spirit of sharing one boat.

sentences.zh: 回奏蒙譴，補牘奚從？

translations.literal: Memorials submitted meet with reproof—what further memorials can follow?
translations.idiomatic: Memorials submitted meet with reproof—what further memorials can follow?

sentences.zh: 內批徑出，封還何自？

translations.literal: Inner drafts issue directly—whence comes returning sealed memorials?
translations.idiomatic: Inner drafts issue directly—whence comes returning sealed memorials?

sentences.zh: 紀綱因循，風俗玩愒。

translations.literal: Discipline drags on, custom grows slack and negligent.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline drags on, and custom grows slack and negligent.

sentences.zh: 功罪罔核，文案徒繁。

translations.literal: Merit and fault go unchecked, paperwork alone grows thick.
translations.idiomatic: Merit and fault go unchecked, and paperwork alone grows thick.

sentences.zh: 閽寺潛為厲階，善類漸以短氣。

translations.literal: Gate attendants secretly serve as stepping-stones to disaster, and good men gradually lose heart.
translations.idiomatic: Gate attendants secretly serve as stepping-stones to disaster, and good men gradually lose heart.

sentences.zh: 言涉宮府，肆撓多端。

translations.literal: Speech touching palace or government is freely obstructed in many ways.
translations.idiomatic: Speech touching palace or government is freely obstructed in many ways.

sentences.zh: 梗在私門，堅持不破。

translations.literal: Obstructions lie in private factions, firmly upheld and never broken.
translations.idiomatic: Obstructions lie in private factions, firmly upheld and never broken.

sentences.zh: 萬眾惶惶，皆謂群小侮常，明良疏隔，自開辟以來，未有若是而永安者。

translations.literal: The myriad people are anxious and fearful; all say petty men scorn norms, ruler and worthy are estranged—and since the beginning of time, none has remained secure forever in such a state.
translations.idiomatic: The people are anxious and fearful; all say petty men scorn norms, ruler and worthy are estranged—and since the beginning of time, none has remained secure forever in such a state.

sentences.zh: 伏願奮英斷以決大計，勿為小故之所淆；

translations.literal: I humbly pray you rouse resolute judgment to decide great policy, and not be confused by petty matters;
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray you rouse resolute judgment to decide great policy, and not be confused by petty matters;

sentences.zh: 弘浚哲以任君子，勿為嬖昵之所惑。

translations.literal: Expand far-seeing wisdom to employ gentlemen, and not be deluded by favorites.
translations.idiomatic: Expand far-seeing wisdom to employ gentlemen, and not be deluded by favorites.

sentences.zh: 移美色奇珍之玩而保瘡痍，分昭陽細務之勤而和庶政。

translations.literal: Shift from delight in beauty and rare treasures to protecting the wounded land; divide the toil of Zhaoyang's minor affairs and harmonize common governance.
translations.idiomatic: Shift from delight in beauty and rare treasures to protecting the wounded land; divide the toil of Zhaoyang's minor affairs and harmonize common governance.

sentences.zh: 以蠻裔為關門勁敵，以錢谷為黎庶脂膏。

translations.literal: Treat frontier peoples as powerful enemies at the strategic passes, and treat money and grain as the fat and marrow squeezed from the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Treat frontier peoples as powerful enemies at the strategic passes, and treat money and grain as the fat and marrow squeezed from the common people.

sentences.zh: 拔用陸樹聲、石星之流，嘉納殷士儋、翁大立諸疏。

translations.literal: Promote men such as Lu Shusheng and Shi Xing; gladly accept the memorials of Yin Shidan, Weng Dali, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Promote men such as Lu Shusheng and Shi Xing; gladly accept the memorials of Yin Shidan, Weng Dali, and others.

sentences.zh: 經史講筵，日親無倦。

translations.literal: At the classics-and-history lecture, attend daily without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: At the classics-and-history lecture, attend daily without weariness.

sentences.zh: 臣民章奏，與所司面相可否。

translations.literal: For memorials of ministers and people, face relevant bureaus in approving or denying them.
translations.idiomatic: For memorials of ministers and people, face the relevant bureaus in approving or denying them.

sentences.zh: 萬幾之裁理漸熟，人才之邪正自知。

translations.literal: Judgment over the myriad affairs will gradually mature, and the upright and corrupt among talent will be known of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Judgment over the myriad affairs will gradually mature, and the upright and corrupt among talent will become known of themselves.

sentences.zh: 察變謹微，回天開泰，計無逾於此。

translations.literal: Discern change and heed the subtle, turn heaven and open prosperity—no plan surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Discern change and heed the subtle, turn heaven and open prosperity—no plan surpasses this.

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝大怒，杖之百，系刑部獄數月。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the emperor was greatly enraged; he was beaten one hundred blows and imprisoned in the Ministry of Justice for several months.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor was greatly enraged; he was beaten one hundred strokes and imprisoned in the Ministry of Justice for several months.

sentences.zh: 刑科舒化等以為言，乃釋為民。

translations.literal: Shu Hua of the Penalties Section and others spoke on his behalf, and he was released as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Hua of the Penalties Section and others spoke on his behalf, and he was released as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，起光祿少卿，卒。

translations.literal: When Shenzong acceded, he was recalled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong acceded, he was recalled as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and died.

sentences.zh: 陳吾德，字懋修，歸善人。

translations.literal: Chen Wude, style Maoxiu, was a native of Guishan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wude, style Maoxiu, was a native of Guishan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-fourth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed courier.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年，擢工科給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longqing he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Works Section.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 3 he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Works Section.

sentences.zh: 兩廣多盜，將吏率虛文罔上。

translations.literal: Guangdong and Guangxi had many bandits, and generals and officials mostly used empty documents to deceive the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong and Guangxi had many bandits, and generals and officials mostly used empty reports to deceive the throne.

sentences.zh: 吾德列便宜八事，皆允行。

translations.literal: Wude listed eight convenient measures, all of which were approved and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Wude listed eight practical measures, all of which were approved and carried out.

sentences.zh: 明年正月朔，日有食之，已而月復食。

translations.literal: On the new moon of the first month of the next year, there was a solar eclipse; soon after, the moon was eclipsed as well.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon of the first month of the next year, there was a solar eclipse; soon after, the moon was eclipsed as well.

sentences.zh: 吾德言：「歲首日月並食，天之大災，陛下宜屏斥一切玩好，應天以實。」

translations.literal: Wude said: "At the year's start sun and moon were both eclipsed—a great calamity from heaven; Your Majesty should dismiss all delights and respond to heaven with substance."
translations.idiomatic: Wude said: "At the year's start sun and moon were both eclipsed—a great calamity from heaven; Your Majesty should dismiss all delights and respond to heaven with substance."

sentences.zh: 詔遣中官督織造，吾德偕同官嚴用和切諫，報聞。

translations.literal: An edict sent eunuchs to supervise weaving and manufacture; Wude together with colleague Yan Yonghe remonstrated urgently, and notice was received.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent eunuchs to supervise weaving and manufacture; Wude and his colleague Yan Yonghe remonstrated urgently, and notice was received.

sentences.zh: 帝從中官崔敏言，命市珍寶，戶部尚書劉體乾、戶科都給事中李已執奏，不從。

translations.literal: The emperor, following eunuch Cui Min's words, ordered the purchase of rare treasures; Minister of Revenue Liu Tigan and Chief Supervising Secretary of the Revenue Section Li Yi submitted firm memorials, but he did not follow them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, following eunuch Cui Min's advice, ordered the purchase of rare treasures; Minister of Revenue Liu Tigan and Chief Supervising Secretary of the Revenue Section Li Yi submitted firm memorials, but he did not follow them.

sentences.zh: 吾德復偕已上疏曰：「伏睹登極詔書，罷采辦，蠲加派，且雲『各監局以缺乏為名，移文苛取，及所司阿附奉行者，言官即時論奏，治以重典』，海內聞之，歡若更生。

translations.literal: Wude again together with Yi submitted a memorial saying: "I have seen the accession edict abolishing procurement, remitting additional levies, and stating that 'where the various directorates and offices, under the pretext of shortage, issue documents to exact harshly, and relevant bureaus fawn and carry out such orders, remonstrance officials shall at once discuss and memorialize, punishing with severe statutes'—when the realm heard this, all rejoiced as if reborn.
translations.idiomatic: Wude again joined Yi in submitting a memorial: "I have seen the accession edict abolishing procurement, remitting additional levies, and stating that 'where the various directorates and offices, under the pretext of shortage, issue documents to exact harshly, and relevant bureaus fawn and carry out such orders, remonstrance officials shall at once discuss and memorialize, punishing with severe statutes'—when the realm heard this, all rejoiced as if reborn.

sentences.zh: 比者左右近習，幹請紛紜，買玉市珠，傳帖數下。

translations.literal: Recently close attendants at your side have made requests in profusion, buying jade and purchasing pearls, with orders transmitted again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Recently close attendants at your side have made requests in profusion, buying jade and purchasing pearls, with orders transmitted again and again.

sentences.zh: 人情惶駭，鹹謂詔書不信，無所適從。

translations.literal: People are anxious and alarmed; all say the edict is not to be believed and there is nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: People are anxious and alarmed; all say the edict cannot be trusted and there is nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 邇時府庫久虛，民生困瘁，司度支者日夕憂危。

translations.literal: Recently the treasury has long been empty, the people's livelihood is exhausted and distressed, and those in charge of revenue day and night worry over danger.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the treasury has long been empty, the people's livelihood is exhausted and distressed, and those in charge of revenue worry day and night over the danger.

sentences.zh: 陛下奈何以玩好故，費數十萬貲乎！

translations.literal: Your Majesty, how can you for the sake of delights spend hundreds of thousands in funds!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, how can you for the sake of delights spend hundreds of thousands in funds!

sentences.zh: 敏等獻諂營私，罪不可宥。

translations.literal: Min and the others offer flattery and pursue private gain—their crime cannot be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Min and the others offer flattery and pursue private gain—their crime cannot be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 乞亟譴斥，以全詔書大信。」

translations.literal: I beg you quickly to reprimand and dismiss them, to preserve the great credibility of the edict."
translations.idiomatic: I beg you quickly to reprimand and dismiss them, to preserve the great credibility of the edict."

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，杖已百，錮刑部獄，斥吾德為民。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged; Yi was beaten one hundred blows and imprisoned in the Ministry of Justice, and Wude was dismissed as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly enraged; Yi was beaten one hundred strokes and imprisoned in the Ministry of Justice, and Wude was dismissed as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 神宗嗣位，起吾德兵科。

translations.literal: When the Shenzong Emperor succeeded, Wude was recalled to the Military Affairs Section.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shenzong Emperor succeeded, Wude was recalled to the Military Affairs Section.

sentences.zh: 萬歷元年，進右給事中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli he was promoted to Right Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 1 he was promoted to Right Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 張居正柄國，諫官言事必先請，吾德獨不往。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng wielded state power; remonstrance officials had to seek permission before speaking on affairs, but Wude alone did not go.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhang Juzheng wielding state power, remonstrance officials had to seek permission before speaking on affairs, but Wude alone refused to do so.

sentences.zh: 禮部主事宋儒與兵部主事熊敦樸不相能，誣敦樸欲劾居正，屬尚書譚綸劾罷之。

translations.literal: Song Ru, a secretary in the Ministry of Rites, and Xiong Dunpu, a secretary in the Ministry of War, were at odds; Ru falsely accused Dunpu of intending to impeach Juzheng and had Minister Tan Lun impeach and dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Song Ru, a secretary in the Ministry of Rites, and Xiong Dunpu, a secretary in the Ministry of War, were at odds; Ru falsely accused Dunpu of intending to impeach Zhang Juzheng and had Minister Tan Lun impeach and dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 既而誣漸白，吾德遂劾儒，亦謫之外。

translations.literal: When the false charge gradually came to light, Wude then impeached Ru, who was also banished abroad.
translations.idiomatic: When the false charge gradually came to light, Wude impeached Ru, who was also banished from court.

sentences.zh: 居正以吾德不白己，嗛之。

translations.literal: Juzheng resented Wude because he had not cleared him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng resented Wude because he had not cleared him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，爭成國公朱希忠贈定襄王爵，益忤居正。

translations.literal: Before long, in the dispute over enfeoffing Marquis of Chengguo Zhu Xizhong posthumously as Prince of Dingxiang, he further offended Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, in the dispute over enfeoffing Zhu Xizhong, Marquis of Chengguo, posthumously as Prince of Dingxiang, he further offended Zhang Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 及慈寧宮後室災，吾德力爭，出為饒州知府。

translations.literal: When fire struck the rear chambers of Cining Palace, Wude argued forcefully and was sent out as prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When fire struck the rear chambers of Cining Palace, Wude argued forcefully and was sent out as prefect of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 有盜建昌王印章者，遁之南京見獲。

translations.literal: A thief who had stolen the seal of the Prince of Jianchang fled to Nanjing and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: A thief who had stolen the seal of the Prince of Jianchang fled to Nanjing and was captured.

sentences.zh: 居正客操江都御史王篆坐吾德部下失盜，謫馬邑典史。

translations.literal: Wang Zhuan, Caojiang regional inspector and Juzheng's client, was held responsible because the thief escaped under Wude's jurisdiction; Wude was demoted to county recorder of Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhuan, Caojiang regional inspector and Zhang Juzheng's client, was held responsible because the thief escaped under Wude's jurisdiction; Wude was demoted to county recorder of Mayi.

sentences.zh: 御史又劾其蒞饒時違制講學，用庫金市學田，遂除名為民。

translations.literal: Censors also impeached him for lecturing in violation of regulations while at Raozhou and using treasury funds to buy school fields; he was then struck from the rolls and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Censors also impeached him for lecturing in violation of regulations while at Raozhou and using treasury funds to buy school fields; he was then struck from the rolls and made a commoner.

sentences.zh: 居正死，薦起思州推官，移寶慶同知，皆以親老不赴。

translations.literal: After Juzheng died, he was recommended and recalled as investigating censor of Sixian and then transferred to administration vice commissioner of Baoxing, but in both cases he did not go because his parents were elderly.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Juzheng died, he was recommended and recalled as investigating censor of Sixian and then transferred to administration vice commissioner of Baoxing, but declined both posts because his parents were elderly.

sentences.zh: 後終湖廣僉事。

translations.literal: He later ended his career as intendant of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He later ended his career as intendant of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 李已，字子復，磁人。

translations.literal: Li Yi, style Zifu, was a native of Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi, style Zifu, was a native of Ci.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-fourth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 除太常博士，擢禮科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was promoted to supervising secretary of the Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was promoted to supervising secretary of the Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中，頻詔戶部有所征索。

translations.literal: During Longqing, edicts frequently ordered the Ministry of Revenue to make levies.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longqing reign, edicts frequently ordered the Ministry of Revenue to make levies.

sentences.zh: 尚書劉體乾輒執奏，已每助之，以是積失帝意。

translations.literal: Minister Liu Tigan repeatedly submitted firm memorials, and Yi always assisted him; by this he gradually lost the emperor's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Liu Tigan repeatedly submitted firm memorials, and Yi always assisted him; by this he gradually lost the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 及爭珍寶事，遂得禍。

translations.literal: When it came to the matter of disputing precious treasures, he thereby met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When the dispute over purchasing precious treasures erupted, disaster followed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，刑科給事中舒化等請釋已，刑部尚書葛守禮等因言：「朝審時，重囚情可矜疑者，鹹得末減。

translations.literal: Before long, Supervising Secretary Shu Hua of the Punishments Section and others requested Yi's release; Minister of Justice Ge Shouli and others then said: "At the Court Review, serious convicts whose circumstances merit compassion or doubt may all receive reduction to lesser penalties.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Supervising Secretary Shu Hua of the Punishments Section and others petitioned for Li Yi's release. Minister of Justice Ge Shouli and others then argued: "At the Court Review, serious offenders whose cases warrant compassion or doubt should all be eligible for commuted sentences.

sentences.zh: 已及內犯張恩等十人，讞未定，不列朝審中。

translations.literal: Yi and the ten inner-palace offenders including Zhang En, whose verdicts were undetermined, were not listed among those in the Court Review.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi and the ten inner-palace offenders, including Zhang En, whose verdicts had not yet been fixed, were excluded from the Court Review altogether.

sentences.zh: 茍瘐死犴狴，將累深仁。」

translations.literal: If they should die of illness in the prison cells, it would encumber deep benevolence."
translations.idiomatic: Should any of them die of illness in custody, it would tarnish Your Majesty's reputation for deep mercy."

sentences.zh: 帝乃釋已，恩等系如故。

translations.literal: The emperor then released Yi; En and the others remained imprisoned as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then released Li Yi alone; Zhang En and the others remained in custody as before.

sentences.zh: 法司以恩等有內援，欲借以脫已。

translations.literal: The judicial offices, believing En and the others had inner-palace backing, wished to use them as a pretext to free Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices assumed that En and the others enjoyed patrons within the palace and hoped to use their case as leverage to secure Li Yi's release.

sentences.zh: 及已獨釋，眾翕然稱帝仁明。

translations.literal: When Yi alone was released, all agreed in acclaiming the emperor as benevolent and wise.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yi alone was freed, the court united in praising the emperor's benevolence and clear judgment.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，薦起兵科都給事中。

translations.literal: When the Shenzong Emperor took the throne, Yi was recommended and raised to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Military Affairs Section.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shenzong Emperor acceded, Li Yi was recommended and appointed Chief Supervising Secretary of the Military Affairs Section.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「陛下初基，弊端盡去，傳奉一事，豈可尚踵故常。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Your Majesty has just taken the foundation; abuses have all been removed—the matter of honorary commissions, how can we still follow the old custom?
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty has only just ascended the throne and swept away longstanding abuses. On the question of honorary commissions, how can we simply carry on as before?

sentences.zh: 內臣即有勤勞，當優以金帛，名器所在，不容濫設。」

translations.literal: Even if inner attendants have rendered service, they should be rewarded with gold and silk; where offices and insignia are concerned, indiscriminate appointment cannot be tolerated."
translations.idiomatic: Even when inner attendants have earned merit, they should be rewarded with gold and silk alone. Offices and insignia must never be handed out indiscriminately."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the proposal and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 御史胡涍建言得罪，已首論救。

translations.literal: Censor Hu Jiao offended the throne by his memorial; Yi was first to speak in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Hu Jiao was punished for a forthright memorial, Li Yi was the first to speak up in his defense.

sentences.zh: 尋劾兵部尚書譚綸去取邊將不當。

translations.literal: Soon he impeached Minister of War Tan Lun for improper selection and dismissal of frontier generals.
translations.idiomatic: He soon impeached Minister of War Tan Lun for mishandling the appointment and removal of frontier generals.

sentences.zh: 平江伯陳王謨罪廢，復夤緣出鎮湖廣，已力爭得寢。

translations.literal: The Earl of Pingjiang Chen Wangmo, convicted and dismissed, again used connections to go out and command Huguang; Yi argued forcefully and had it shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The Earl of Pingjiang, Chen Wangmo, though convicted and dismissed, again used connections to secure a command in Huguang. Li Yi fought the appointment vigorously and had it blocked.

sentences.zh: 擢順天府丞，遷大理右少卿。

translations.literal: Promoted to vice magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture, then transferred to Right Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture and later transferred to Right Assistant Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 疏請改父母誥命，日已暮，逼禁門守者投入。

translations.literal: In a memorial he requested alteration of his parents' patent of nobility; the day was already late, so he pressed the gate guards to let it in.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial requesting changes to his parents' patent of nobility. The hour was late, so he pressed the palace gate guards to accept it anyway.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謫常州同知。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered and demoted him to vice prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and demoted him to vice prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，已與吾德並敢言，已尤以直著。

translations.literal: Initially Yi and Wude were both outspoken, but Yi was especially noted for bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: At first Li Yi and Chen Wude were both known for speaking boldly, but Yi was especially famed for his bluntness.

sentences.zh: 兩遭摧抑，頗事營進。

translations.literal: Having twice suffered setback and suppression, he came to devote himself somewhat to advancement.
translations.idiomatic: After suffering two crushing setbacks, he turned increasingly to scheming for promotion.

sentences.zh: 後為南京考功郎中。

translations.literal: Later he served as bureau director of merit evaluation in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He later became bureau director of merit evaluation in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 九年京察，希張居正指，與尚書何寬置司業張位、長史趙世卿察典，遂得擢南京尚寶卿。

translations.literal: In the ninth year's metropolitan evaluation, reading Zhang Juzheng's hints, together with Minister He Kuan he placed Vice Director of Studies Zhang Wei and chief steward Zhao Shiqing in charge of the review, and thereby won promotion to Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: During the ninth year's metropolitan evaluation, taking his cue from Zhang Juzheng, he joined Minister He Kuan in putting Vice Director of Studies Zhang Wei and chief steward Zhao Shiqing in charge of the review. By this maneuver he won promotion to Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 三遷右僉都御史，巡撫保定六府。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, grand coordinator of the six prefectures of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: After three further promotions he became Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of the six prefectures of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 逾年，罷歸，卒。

translations.literal: After a year he was dismissed and returned home, then died.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was dismissed, returned home, and died.

sentences.zh: 胡涍，字原荊，無錫人。

translations.literal: Hu Jiao, style Yuanjing, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Jiao, styled Yuanjing, came from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖末舉進士。

translations.literal: At the end of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination near the end of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 歷知永豐、安福二縣，擢御史。

translations.literal: He served in succession as magistrate of Yongfeng and Anfu counties, then was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as magistrate of Yongfeng and Anfu counties before being promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位之六日，命馮保代孟沖掌司禮監，召用南京守備張宏。

translations.literal: On the sixth day after the Shenzong Emperor's accession, Feng Bao was ordered to replace Meng Chong as director of the Directorate of Ceremonial, and Zhang Hong, the Nanjing garrison commander, was summoned to office.
translations.idiomatic: Six days after the Shenzong Emperor's accession, Feng Bao was ordered to replace Meng Chong as director of the Directorate of Ceremonial, and Zhang Hong, the Nanjing garrison commander, was recalled to office.

sentences.zh: 涍請嚴馭近習，毋惑諂諛，虧損聖德。

translations.literal: Jiao requested strict control of close attendants, that they not be misled by flattery and sycophancy to the detriment of sage virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao urged the emperor to keep his close attendants under strict discipline, lest flattery and sycophancy erode his moral authority.

sentences.zh: 保大怒，思傾之。

translations.literal: Feng was greatly angered and sought to bring him down.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was furious and set about trying to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 其冬，妖星見，慈寧宮後延燒連房。

translations.literal: That winter an ominous star appeared, and a fire behind Cining Palace spread through connected buildings.
translations.idiomatic: That winter an ominous star appeared, and a fire behind Cining Palace spread through a row of adjoining buildings.

sentences.zh: 涍乞遍察掖廷中曾蒙先朝寵幸者，體恤優遇，其余無論老少，一概放遣。

translations.literal: Jiao asked for a thorough investigation of all in the rear palaces who had once enjoyed former imperial favor, that they be treated with consideration and preferment; the rest, regardless of age, should one and all be released and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao petitioned for a thorough review of every woman in the rear palaces who had once enjoyed the late emperor's favor, that they be treated with kindness and care. All the rest, young or old alike, should be released and sent away.

sentences.zh: 奏中有「唐高不君，則天為虐」語。

translations.literal: The memorial contained the phrases "Gaozu of Tang was no proper ruler, and Wu Zetian was cruel."
translations.idiomatic: The memorial included the lines "Gaozu of Tang was no true sovereign, and Wu Zetian was a tyrant."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，問輔臣，二語所指為誰。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and asked the chief ministers whom the two phrases referred to.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and asked his chief ministers whom the two phrases were meant to describe.

sentences.zh: 張居正對曰：「涍言雖狂悖，心無他。」

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng replied: "Though Jiao's words are wild and rebellious, his heart harbors no other intent."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng replied: "Jiao's language may be reckless and disrespectful, but his heart is not disloyal."

sentences.zh: 帝意未釋，嚴旨譙讓。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger was not yet dispelled, and a stern edict rebuked and reproved him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger did not subside, and a stern edict rebuked Jiao sharply.

sentences.zh: 涍惶恐請罪，斥為民。

translations.literal: Jiao in fear requested punishment and was reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao, terrified, begged forgiveness and was stripped of office and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 逾年，巡按御史李學詩薦涍。

translations.literal: After a year, Regional Investigating Censor Li Xueshi recommended Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, Regional Investigating Censor Li Xueshi recommended Jiao for office.

sentences.zh: 詔自後有薦者，並逮治涍。

translations.literal: An edict declared that henceforth anyone who recommended him would also be seized and punished along with Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that from then on anyone who recommended him would be seized and punished along with Jiao.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Many years later, he died.

sentences.zh: 汪文輝，字德充，婺源人。

translations.literal: Wang Wenhui, style Dechong, was a native of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenhui, styled Dechong, came from Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-fourth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授工部主事。

translations.literal: Appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He received appointment as a secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 隆慶四年，改御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Longqing, he transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 4 he transferred to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 高拱以內閣掌吏部，權勢烜赫。

translations.literal: Gao Gong held the Ministry of Personnel from the inner cabinet, and his power and influence blazed brilliantly.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong controlled the Ministry of Personnel from within the inner cabinet, and his power and influence were dazzling.

sentences.zh: 其門生韓楫、宋之韓、程文、塗夢桂等並居言路，日夜走其門，專務搏擊。

translations.literal: His disciples Han Ji, Song Zhihan, Cheng Wen, Tu Menggui, and others all held posts on the remonstrance circuit; day and night they ran to his door, devoting themselves solely to attacks and impeachments.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples Han Ji, Song Zhihan, Cheng Wen, Tu Menggui, and others all held remonstrance posts. Day and night they flocked to his door, devoting themselves entirely to denunciations and impeachments.

sentences.zh: 文輝亦拱門生，心獨非之。

translations.literal: Wenhui was also Gao's disciple, but in his heart alone disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhui was also Gao's disciple, but he alone disapproved in his heart.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，疏陳四事，專責言官。

translations.literal: The following year in the second month, he submitted a memorial setting forth four matters, laying blame specifically on the remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: The following February he submitted a memorial outlining four abuses, placing the blame squarely on the remonstrance officials.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：

translations.literal: The gist read:
translations.idiomatic: The gist of it read:

sentences.zh: 先帝末年所任大臣，本協恭濟務，無少釁嫌。

translations.literal: The great ministers the late emperor appointed in his final years were originally harmonious in their joint service, with not the slightest friction.
translations.idiomatic: The great ministers the late emperor appointed in his final years worked together in harmony, without the slightest hint of discord.

sentences.zh: 始於一二言官見廟堂議論稍殊，遂潛察低昂、窺所向而攻其所忌。

translations.literal: It began when one or two remonstrance officials, seeing that court deliberation differed slightly, secretly observed who was rising or falling, watched which way things leaned, and attacked those they resented.
translations.idiomatic: It began when one or two remonstrance officials, noticing slight differences in court deliberation, secretly tracked who was rising and who was falling, watched which way the wind blew, and attacked those they resented.

sentences.zh: 致顛倒是非，熒惑聖聽，傷國家大體。

translations.literal: This led to the inversion of right and wrong, bewildered the imperial ear, and harmed the fundamental integrity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The result was the inversion of right and wrong, the bewildering of the imperial ear, and grave damage to the fundamental interests of the state.

sentences.zh: 茍踵承前弊，交煽並構，使正人不安其位，恐宋元祐之禍，復見於今，是為傾陷。

translations.literal: If we continue the former abuses, colluding to incite and fabricate charges together so that upright men cannot rest secure in their posts—I fear the disaster of the Yuanyou era may reappear today. This is what I call entrapment.
translations.idiomatic: If these old abuses continue—officials colluding to incite one another and fabricate charges until upright men cannot hold their posts—I fear the catastrophe of the Yuanyou era may return in our own day. This I call entrapment.

sentences.zh: 祖宗立法，至精密矣，而卒有不行者，非法敝也，不得其人耳。

translations.literal: Our forefathers' laws were made with the utmost precision, yet in the end some went unenforced—not because the laws were flawed, but because the right men were not in place.
translations.idiomatic: The laws our forefathers established were precise to the last detail, yet some still went unenforced—not because the laws themselves were defective, but because the right men were not appointed to carry them out.

sentences.zh: 今言官條奏，率銳意更張。

translations.literal: Today remonstrance officials' itemized memorials invariably seek bold reform and change.
translations.idiomatic: Today remonstrance officials' itemized memorials invariably push for sweeping reforms.

sentences.zh: 部臣重違言官，輕變祖制，遷就一時，茍且允覆。

translations.literal: Ministry officials, dreading to oppose the remonstrance officials, lightly alter ancestral institutions, yielding for the moment and granting perfunctory approval.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry officials, afraid to cross the remonstrance officials, lightly alter ancestral institutions, yielding to the moment and granting perfunctory approval.

sentences.zh: 及法立弊起，又議復舊。

translations.literal: When the new law is established and abuses arise, they debate restoring the old ways.
translations.idiomatic: Once the new law is in place and new abuses appear, they debate restoring the old system.

sentences.zh: 政非通變之宜，民無畫一之守，是為紛更。

translations.literal: Government lacks the fitness of flexible adaptation, and the people have no single standard to follow. This is what I call chaotic alternation.
translations.idiomatic: Government loses the virtue of measured adaptation, and the people have no consistent rule to live by. This I call chaotic alternation.

sentences.zh: 古大臣坐事退者，必為微其詞；

translations.literal: In antiquity when great ministers retired because of an affair, their wording was invariably softened;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when great ministers stepped down because of a scandal, their memorials always softened the language;

sentences.zh: 所以養廉恥，存國體。

translations.literal: this was to nurture integrity and shame and preserve the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: this was done to preserve their honor and the dignity of the state.

sentences.zh: 今或掇其已往，揣彼未形，逐景循聲，爭相詬病，若市井喧哄然。

translations.literal: Now some dredge up what is past, surmise what has not yet taken form, chase shadows and follow rumors, competing to revile and find fault—as noisy as a marketplace uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Now some dredge up the distant past, surmise offenses not yet committed, chase shadows and follow rumors, and compete in reviling and finding fault—as clamorous as a marketplace brawl.

sentences.zh: 至方面重臣，茍非甚奸慝，亦宜棄短錄長，為人才惜。

translations.literal: As for regional heavyweights, unless they are extremely wicked, one should set aside faults and record merits, cherishing talent for the state's sake.
translations.idiomatic: As for regional heavyweights, unless they are utterly corrupt, one should overlook their faults and value their strengths, cherishing talent for the state's sake.

sentences.zh: 今或搜抉小疵，指為大蠹，極言醜詆，使決引去。

translations.literal: Now some hunt out minor flaws, call them great corruption, vilify to the utmost, and force resolute departure.
translations.idiomatic: Now some hunt out minor flaws, declare them grave corruption, vilify their targets without restraint, and drive them to resign.

sentences.zh: 以此求人，國家安得全才而用之？

translations.literal: Seeking men on such terms, how can the state obtain complete talent and employ it?
translations.idiomatic: If this is how we search for talent, how can the state find capable men in full measure and put them to use?

sentences.zh: 是為苛刻。

translations.literal: This is what I call harsh severity.
translations.idiomatic: This I call harsh severity.

sentences.zh: 言官能規切人主，糾彈大臣。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials can admonish and correct the ruler and impeach great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials may admonish the ruler and impeach great ministers.

sentences.zh: 至言官之短，誰為指之者？

translations.literal: But as for the remonstrance officials' own faults—who points them out?
translations.idiomatic: But when remonstrance officials themselves fall short, who is there to call them to account?

sentences.zh: 今言事論人或不當，部臣不為奏覆，即憤然不平；

translations.literal: Now when their submissions discussing others are improper and ministry officials do not transmit a reply, they become instantly indignant;
translations.idiomatic: Nowadays, when a remonstrance official's accusation misses the mark and a ministry does not relay a formal reply, he flies into a rage at once;

sentences.zh: 雖同列明知其非，亦莫與辨，以為體貌當如是。

translations.literal: even colleagues who clearly know they are wrong do not argue with them, thinking such bearing is only fitting.
translations.idiomatic: even colleagues who know perfectly well that he is in the wrong refuse to argue with him, believing such deference is only proper.

sentences.zh: 夫臣子且不肯一言受過，何以責難君父哉？

translations.literal: If even as subjects they will not accept a single word of fault, how can we demand reproach of the ruler and father?
translations.idiomatic: If even as subjects they will not accept a single word of criticism, how can we expect them to hold the ruler himself to account?

sentences.zh: 是為求勝。

translations.literal: This is what I call striving for victory.
translations.idiomatic: This I call striving for victory.

sentences.zh: 此四弊者，今日所當深戒。

translations.literal: These four abuses are what must be deeply guarded against today.
translations.idiomatic: These four abuses are precisely what the court must guard against today.

sentences.zh: 然其要在大臣取鑒前失，勿用希指生事之人。

translations.literal: Yet the key lies in great ministers learning from past failures and not employing men who seize upon hints to stir trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the heart of the matter is that great ministers must learn from past mistakes and refuse to employ men who seize upon hints to manufacture trouble.

sentences.zh: 希指生事之人進，則忠直貞諒之士遠，而頌成功、譽盛德者日至於前。

translations.literal: When men who seize hints to stir trouble advance, loyal, upright, and sincere men keep their distance, while those who praise achievements and extol great virtue arrive daily before one's eyes.
translations.idiomatic: When men who seize upon hints to stir trouble rise to power, loyal and upright men keep their distance, while flatterers praising every achievement and extolling every virtue arrive daily at one's door.

sentences.zh: 大臣任己專斷，即有闕失，孰從聞之？

translations.literal: If great ministers act on their own with arbitrary judgment, even when there are faults and omissions, who will hear of them?
translations.idiomatic: If great ministers act on their own authority, who will ever hear of their faults and failures?

sentences.zh: 蓋宰相之職，不當以救時自足，當以格心為本。

translations.literal: For the chancellor's duty is not to be satisfied with merely rescuing the age—it should take rectifying the heart as its foundation.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor's duty is not merely to rescue the times; it is, above all, to rectify the ruler's heart.

sentences.zh: 願陛下明飭中外，消朋比之私，還淳厚之俗，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will clearly admonish court and countryside, dispel the private bonds of faction, and restore the wholesome custom; great fortune for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty will clearly admonish court and countryside alike, dissolve the private bonds of faction, and restore a wholesome custom to the realm. All under Heaven would be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，下所司。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and forwarded to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and forwarded to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 拱惡其刺己，甫三日，出為寧夏僉事。

translations.literal: Gong hated its barb against himself; within three days Wenhui was sent out as administration vice commissioner of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong resented its implicit attack on him. Within three days Wenhui was sent out to serve as administration vice commissioner of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 修屯政，蠲浮糧，建水閘，流亡漸歸。

translations.literal: He repaired the garrison-farm system, remitted excess grain levies, built sluice gates, and exiles gradually returned.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the garrison-farm system, remitted excess grain levies, built sluice gates, and refugees gradually returned home.

sentences.zh: 御史富平孫丕揚忤拱，為希指者所劾。

translations.literal: Censor Sun Piyang of Fuping offended Gong and was impeached by those who seized upon hints.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Sun Piyang of Fuping offended Gao Gong and was impeached by those who seized upon hints to do his bidding.

sentences.zh: 方行勘，文輝抗言曰：「毛舉細故，齮龁正人，以快當路之私，我固不肯為，諸君亦不可也。」

translations.literal: Just as the investigation was proceeding, Wenhui protested: "Raising petty particulars, gnawing at upright men to gratify the private wishes of those in power—I will not do it, and you must not either."
translations.idiomatic: Just as the investigation was underway, Wenhui spoke out: "Raising petty charges and gnawing at upright men to gratify those in power—I will never do it, and neither should you."

sentences.zh: 於是緩其事。

translations.literal: The matter was thus slowed.
translations.idiomatic: The investigation was accordingly slowed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，劾者先得罪去，丕揚竟獲免。

translations.literal: Before long the accusers were first punished and removed, and Piyang ultimately escaped unscathed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the accusers were themselves punished and dismissed, and Sun Piyang ultimately escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 神宗嗣位，拱罷政，召為尚寶卿。

translations.literal: When the Shenzong Emperor succeeded, Gong left office, and Wenhui was summoned as Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shenzong Emperor succeeded to the throne and Gao Gong left office, Wenhui was recalled as Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 尋告歸。

translations.literal: Soon he requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon requested leave to retire home.

sentences.zh: 久之，有詔召用。

translations.literal: After a long while, an edict summoned him back to service.
translations.idiomatic: Many years later, an edict summoned him back to office.

sentences.zh: 未赴卒。

translations.literal: Before he could go, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, he died.

sentences.zh: 劉奮庸，洛陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Fenyong, a native of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fenyong came from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十八年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授兵部主事。

translations.literal: Appointed a secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He received appointment as a secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 尋改禮部兼翰林待詔。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to the Ministry of Rites, concurrently a Hanlin awaiting-imperial-call.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of Rites, concurrently serving as a Hanlin awaiting-imperial-call.

sentences.zh: 侍穆宗裕邸。

translations.literal: He attended the Future Emperor Muzong in the Prince of Yu's residence.
translations.idiomatic: He served the future Emperor Muzong in the Prince of Yu's household.

sentences.zh: 進員外郎。

translations.literal: Promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the rank of vice director.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，以舊恩，擢尚寶卿。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, out of old favor he was promoted to Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne, Fenyong was promoted to Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia in recognition of their old bond.

sentences.zh: 已，藩邸舊臣相繼柄用，獨奮庸久不調。

translations.literal: Before long, old companions from the princely residence were successively wielding power; Fenyong alone went long without reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, old companions from the princely household were put in power one after another, while Fenyong alone went long without a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 大學士高拱亦故官也，再起任事，頗專恣，奮庸疾之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Gao Gong was also a former companion; recalled to duty, he was rather domineering and self-willed, and Fenyong resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Gao Gong was also a former companion from the princely household. Recalled to office, he grew domineering and self-willed, and Fenyong deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 隆慶六年三月，上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year of Longqing, he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Longqing 6 he submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 陛下踐阼六載，朝綱若振飭，而大柄漸移；

translations.literal: Your Majesty has been on the throne six years; court discipline seems restored, yet the great handle of power is gradually shifting;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has reigned six years. Court discipline seems restored, yet the levers of power are gradually slipping away;

sentences.zh: 仕路若肅清，而積習仍故。

translations.literal: the official career seems cleansed, yet entrenched habits remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: the official ranks seem cleansed, yet entrenched habits remain unchanged.

sentences.zh: 百僚方引領以睹勵精之治，而陛下精神誌意漸不逮初。

translations.literal: The hundred officials are craning their necks to behold a reign of invigorated diligence, yet Your Majesty's spirit and resolution gradually fall short of what they were at the start.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred officials are craning their necks in hope of a reign of renewed vigor, yet Your Majesty's spirit and resolve are gradually falling short of what they were at the beginning.

sentences.zh: 臣念潛邸舊恩，誼不忍默。

translations.literal: Your subject, mindful of the old favor of the hidden residence, cannot in duty remain silent.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of the old favor of the prince's household, your subject cannot in conscience remain silent.

sentences.zh: 謹條五事，以俟英斷。

translations.literal: I respectfully set forth five matters, awaiting Your resolute judgment.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully lay out five matters for Your resolute judgment.

sentences.zh: 一、保聖躬。

translations.literal: First, preserve the sacred person.
translations.idiomatic: First, preserve the sacred person of the ruler.

sentences.zh: 人主一身，天地人神之主，必誌氣清明，精神完固，而後可以禦萬幾。

translations.literal: The ruler's person is lord of Heaven, Earth, and the spirits; his will and spirit must be clear and whole before he can govern the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's person is lord of Heaven, Earth, and the spirits; his will and spirit must be clear and whole before he can govern the myriad affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 望凝神定誌，忍性抑情，毋逞旦夕之娛，毋徇無涯之欲，則無疆之福可長保也。

translations.literal: I pray you concentrate the spirit and settle the will, restrain nature and suppress emotion, indulge neither momentary pleasure nor boundless desire—then boundless blessing may be long preserved.
translations.idiomatic: I pray you concentrate your spirit and settle your will, restrain your nature and master your passions, indulge neither momentary pleasure nor boundless desire—then boundless blessing may be long preserved.

sentences.zh: 二、總大權。

translations.literal: Second, gather supreme authority.
translations.idiomatic: Second, gather supreme authority in your own hands.

sentences.zh: 今政府所擬議，百司所承行，非不奉詔旨，而其間從違之故，陛下曾獨斷否乎？

translations.literal: Today what the government deliberates and the hundred offices carry out does not fail to follow imperial edict—yet among the reasons for compliance or refusal, has Your Majesty ever judged alone?
translations.idiomatic: Today what the government deliberates and the hundred offices carry out does follow imperial edict—yet among the reasons for compliance or refusal, has Your Majesty ever judged alone?

sentences.zh: 國事之更張，人才之用舍，未必盡出忠謀，協公論。

translations.literal: Changes in state affairs and the appointment or dismissal of talent do not necessarily all spring from loyal counsel and accord with public judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Changes in state affairs and the appointment or dismissal of talent do not necessarily all spring from loyal counsel or accord with public judgment.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下躬攬大權，凡庶府建白，閣臣擬旨，特留清覽，時出獨斷，則臣下莫能測其機，而政柄不致旁落矣。

translations.literal: Your subject prays that Your Majesty personally hold great authority: for every proposal from the ministries and every draft rescript from the Grand Secretariat, specially reserve them for clear perusal and from time to time render independent judgment—then subjects cannot fathom your intent and the handle of government will not fall to others.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject prays that Your Majesty personally hold great authority: for every proposal from the ministries and every draft rescript from the Grand Secretariat, reserve them for your own clear reading and from time to time render independent judgment—then subjects cannot fathom your intent and the handle of government will not slip from your grasp.

sentences.zh: 三、慎儉德。

translations.literal: Third, be careful in frugal virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Third, guard frugal virtue with care.

sentences.zh: 陛下嗣位以來，傳旨取銀不下數十萬，求珍異之寶，作鰲山之燈，服禦器用，悉鏤金雕玉。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty succeeded, edicts ordering silver have totaled no less than several hundred thousand taels; rare treasures have been sought, Tortoise Mountain lamps made, and imperial garments and utensils all carved in gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty succeeded, edicts ordering silver have totaled no less than several hundred thousand taels; rare treasures have been sought, Tortoise Mountain lamps made, and imperial garments and utensils all carved in gold and jade.

sentences.zh: 生財甚難，靡敝無紀。

translations.literal: Wealth is hard to produce, yet waste is without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth is hard to produce, yet waste knows no limit.

sentences.zh: 願察內帑之空虛，思小民之艱苦，不作無益，不貴異物，則國用充羨，而民樂其生矣。

translations.literal: I pray you observe the emptiness of the inner treasury, reflect on the hardship of the common people, undertake nothing useless, and prize no exotic things—then state revenue will be ample and the people will rejoice in their lives.
translations.idiomatic: I pray you observe the emptiness of the inner treasury, reflect on the hardship of the common people, undertake nothing useless, and prize no exotic things—then state revenue will be ample and the people will rejoice in their lives.

sentences.zh: 四、覽章奏。

translations.literal: Fourth, peruse memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, read memorials attentively.

sentences.zh: 人臣進言，豈能皆當。

translations.literal: When ministers offer counsel, how can it all be right?
translations.idiomatic: When ministers offer counsel, how can it all be right?

sentences.zh: 陛下一切置不覽，非惟虛忠良獻納之誠，抑恐權奸蔽壅，勢自此成。

translations.literal: Your Majesty sets them all aside unread—not only rendering vain the sincere offerings of loyal men, but also allowing powerful traitors to block and choke off access, and the momentum for this begins here.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty sets them all aside unread—not only rendering vain the sincere offerings of loyal men, but also allowing powerful traitors to block and choke off access, and the momentum for this begins here.

sentences.zh: 望陛下留神章奏，曲垂容納。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will attend to memorials and graciously accept them.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will attend to memorials and graciously accept them.

sentences.zh: 言及君德，則反己自修；

translations.literal: When counsel touches the ruler's virtue, turn back and cultivate yourself;
translations.idiomatic: When counsel touches the ruler's virtue, turn back and cultivate yourself;

sentences.zh: 言及朝政，則更化善治。

translations.literal: when it touches court government, then reform and govern well.
translations.idiomatic: when it touches court government, then reform and govern well.

sentences.zh: 聽言者既見之行事，而進言者益樂於效忠矣。

translations.literal: Those who hear counsel will see it put into action, and those who offer counsel will be all the more glad to serve loyally.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hear counsel will see it put into action, and those who offer counsel will be all the more glad to serve loyally.

sentences.zh: 五、用忠直。

translations.literal: Fifth, employ the loyal and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, employ loyal and upright men.

sentences.zh: 邇歲進諫者，或以勤政，或以節用，或以進賢退不肖，此皆無所利而為之；

translations.literal: In recent years those who remonstrated did so for diligent government, or frugality, or advancing the worthy and removing the unworthy—all acted without personal gain;
translations.idiomatic: In recent years those who remonstrated did so for diligent government, or frugality, or advancing the worthy and removing the unworthy—all acted without personal gain;

sentences.zh: 非若承望風旨，肆攻擊以雪他人之憤，迎合權要，交薦拔以樹淫朋之黨者比也。

translations.literal: they are not like those who watch the wind of power, attack freely to vent others' anger, curry favor with the mighty, and recommend one another to build factions of corrupt associates.
translations.idiomatic: they are not like those who watch the wind of power, attack freely to vent others' anger, curry favor with the mighty, and recommend one another to build factions of corrupt associates.

sentences.zh: 願恕狂愚之罪，嘉批鱗之誠，登之有位，以作士氣，則讜規日聞，裨益非鮮。

translations.literal: I pray you pardon my rash folly, honor the sincerity of touching the dragon's scales, place such men in office to revive scholarly morale—then forthright counsel will daily be heard and the benefit will be no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: I pray you pardon my rash folly, honor the sincerity of touching the dragon's scales, place such men in office to revive scholarly morale—then forthright counsel will daily be heard and the benefit will be no small matter.

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝但報聞，不怒也。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor merely acknowledged receipt and was not angry.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor merely acknowledged receipt and was not angry.

sentences.zh: 而附拱者謂奮庸久不徙官，怏怏風刺，相與詆訾之。

translations.literal: Those attached to Gong said Fenyong had long gone without transfer of office and, resentful, offered veiled satire; they joined in slandering him.
translations.idiomatic: Gong's supporters said Fenyong had long gone without a new appointment and, resentful, offered veiled satire; they joined in denouncing him.

sentences.zh: 給事中塗夢桂遂劾奮庸動搖國是。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Tu Menggui then impeached Fenyong for shaking the national policy.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Tu Menggui then impeached Fenyong for undermining state policy.

sentences.zh: 會給事中曹大埜亦劾拱十罪，帝斥之。

translations.literal: At the same time Supervising Secretary Cao Dayan also impeached Gong on ten charges; the emperor rebuffed him.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Supervising Secretary Cao Dayan also impeached Gao Gong on ten charges; the emperor rebuffed him.

sentences.zh: 給事中程文因奏拱竭忠報國，萬世永賴，奮庸與大埜漸構奸謀，傾陷元輔，罪不可勝誅。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Cheng Wen thereupon memorialized that Gong had exhausted loyalty in serving the state and would be relied upon for ten thousand generations, while Fenyong and Dayan were gradually weaving treacherous plots to topple the chief minister—crimes beyond numbering for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Cheng Wen thereupon memorialized that Gong had served the state with utter loyalty and would be relied upon for ages, while Fenyong and Dayan were gradually weaving treacherous plots to topple the chief minister—crimes beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 章並下吏部。

translations.literal: The memorials were all sent down to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials were all sent down to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 拱方掌部事，陽為二臣祈寬。

translations.literal: Gong was then in charge of the ministry and outwardly pleaded leniency for the two officials.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong was then in charge of the ministry and outwardly pleaded leniency for the two officials.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，竟謫大埜乾州判官，奮庸興國知州。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it and ultimately demoted Dayan to judge of Qianzhou and Fenyong to prefect of Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not agree and ultimately demoted Dayan to judge of Qianzhou and Fenyong to prefect of Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 夢桂、文皆拱門生。

translations.literal: Menggui and Wen were both Gong's disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Menggui and Wen were both Gao Gong's disciples.

sentences.zh: 夢桂極詆奮庸，文則盛稱頌拱，又盡舉大埜奏中語代拱剖析，士論非之。

translations.literal: Menggui denounced Fenyong to the utmost; Wen lavishly praised Gong and also repeated in full the words of Dayan's memorial to analyze on Gong's behalf—scholarly opinion condemned this.
translations.idiomatic: Menggui denounced Fenyong to the utmost; Wen lavishly praised Gong and also repeated Dayan's entire memorial to argue Gong's case on his behalf—public opinion condemned them.

sentences.zh: 奮庸謫官兩月，會神宗即位，遂擢山西提學僉事。

translations.literal: Two months after Fenyong was demoted, the Shenzong Emperor succeeded to the throne, and he was then promoted to education intendant of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Two months after Fenyong was demoted, the Shenzong Emperor succeeded to the throne, and Fenyong was promoted to education intendant of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 再遷陜西提學副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to education vice commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to education vice commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 以病乞歸，卒。

translations.literal: He begged leave to return home on grounds of illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: He begged leave to return home on grounds of illness and died.

sentences.zh: 大埜，巴縣人。

translations.literal: Dayan was a native of Baxian.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Dayan came from Baxian.

sentences.zh: 其劾拱，張居正實使之。

translations.literal: His impeachment of Gong was in fact instigated by Zhang Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: His impeachment of Gao Gong was in fact instigated by Zhang Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，累遷右副都御史，巡撫江西。

translations.literal: In the Wanli years he was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli years he rose repeatedly to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 以貪劾免。

translations.literal: He was impeached for greed and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached for corruption and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：世宗之季，門戶漸開。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: In the late years of the Jiajing Emperor, factional gates gradually opened.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser says: In the late years of Emperor Jiajing, factional gates gradually opened.

sentences.zh: 居言路者，各有所主，故其時不患其不言，患其言之冗漫無當，與其心之不能無私；

translations.literal: Those who held the remonstrance path each had their patrons; thus the age did not worry that they would not speak, but that their words were prolix, diffuse, and beside the point, and that their hearts could not be without private motive;
translations.idiomatic: Those who held the remonstrance path each had their patrons; thus the age did not worry that they would not speak, but that their words were prolix, diffuse, and beside the point, and that their hearts could not be without private motive;

sentences.zh: 言愈多，而國是愈益淆亂也。

translations.literal: the more they spoke, the more confused the national consensus became.
translations.idiomatic: the more they spoke, the more confused the national consensus became.

sentences.zh: 汪文輝所陳四弊，有旨哉！

translations.literal: The four abuses set forth by Wang Wenhui—how pointed they were!
translations.idiomatic: The four abuses set forth by Wang Wenhui—how pointed they were!

sentences.zh: 論明季言路諸臣，而考其得失，當於是觀之。

translations.literal: In discussing the remonstrance officials of the late Ming and weighing their gains and losses, one should take this as the measure.
translations.idiomatic: In discussing the remonstrance officials of the late Ming and weighing their gains and losses, one should take this as the measure.
